  several deliveries now puts each delivery's part of its premium into
  the average-cost pool when that delivery comes (per share; the last
  delivery brings what is left). A sale between deliveries no longer has
  the whole premium taken out of it (TJ-0673).
- Canadian `tjs stats` / `tjs win-rates`: a split that only one broker
  records now splits every taxable account's pooled shares, as the
  books' one pool does. The premium's part of a later sale was figured
  on too few shares (TJ-0682).
- Canadian `tjs stats` / `tjs win-rates`: an assigned put's premium is
  now replayed through the pool in the books' own order, settlement date
  first whatever `tax_date` says. A purchase traded before a sale but
  settling after it no longer takes part of the premium that sale
  carries (TJ-0683).

### Fixed: elect

- `tjs elect ACCOUNT --json` lists the events the sheltered default
  booked, as `tjs elect --json` does. A manifest.json that cannot be
  read made `tjs elect [ACCOUNT] --json` exit 0; it prints the account's
  `error` and exits 2, and the text listing exits 2 too (was 1).
  (TJ-0400, TJ-0406)
- `tjs elect --pending ACCOUNT` lists only that account's pending
  elections. It refuses `--set`, `--hint`, `--redo`, `--reset` or
  `--event` beside it, and `--event` without `--redo` / `--reset`; every
  refused flag exits 2 (a usage error), not 1. `tjs elect --set` saves
  only an election the project's country knows: a stale
  work/pending_elections.json that offers the other country's options is
  read again from the exports or refused, so a US project can no longer
  save a Canadian rollover. (TJ-0539, TJ-0540)
- Two `tjs elect` commands (or elect and a run's prompt) running at once
  both keep their election: the manifest's load, change and save happen
  under a lock, the hidden file `.manifest.json.lock` beside it.
  (TJ-0544)
- `tjs elect --redo` clears nothing it cannot ask about again. It is
  refused when the account has no corporate-action export or `--event`
  names an event no export holds, it keeps elections of events no export
  holds, and it puts back what it cleared if interrupted. (TJ-0556)
- docs/commands.md documents `tjs elect --pending --json`: `summary`
  names the shares delivered, and `qty_received`, the ratio fields and
  the cash-in-lieu fields give the fraction paid in cash. (TJ-0222)

### Fixed: inputs, init and the shared layout

- In the shared layout (`inputs_dir = "../inputs"`), `tjs run` skipped a
  spreadsheet export and a subfolder of exports with no message, leaving
  their trades out. It checks the shared folder as it checks a local
  inputs/: a spreadsheet stops the run, and a subfolder of exports is
  named with the fix. (TJ-0482, TJ-0582)
- A NAME.redacted.csv (or .tt) copy that `taxjson redact FILE` wrote
  beside its export in inputs/ was read too, booking the account's rows
  twice. It is no longer read, and a warning names it. (TJ-0476)
- An export with only a header (a period with no activity) is an Info
  line, not a warning that left run-clean and `tjs sum` flagged for
  good, and a file whose rows book nothing names the file check to do as
  run-clean's fix. (TJ-0483)
- The check run on every parsed row refuses a date that is not a
  calendar day (2025-02-30) and a NaN, infinite or non-numeric amount or
  quantity, which passed as clean output. (TJ-0522)
- `taxjson-xlsx-to-csv` writes each cell as the sheet shows it: a label
  given twice stays twice for the parser to refuse, and an id formatted
  with leading zeros keeps them; `--sheet 2025` selects the sheet named
  2025 before index 2025. getting-started, brokers.md and the
  inputs/<account>/README.txt that init writes say the converter needs
  the optional xlsx extra and give the installer line
  (`TAXJSON_EXTRAS=fx,xlsx`), and the missing-extra error starts with
  it. (TJ-0534, TJ-0535, TJ-0536, TJ-0425)
- `tjs init` checks the year's holdings folder before it writes
  anything, and if a write fails later a new project's files are
  removed, so the retry is not refused with "taxjson.toml already
  exists". `init --year` of an earlier year beside existing year folders
  names no taxjson.toml.bak it did not write, makes no template account
  folder in the shared inputs/, and names the year whose `[accounts.*]`
  tables to copy. (TJ-0568, TJ-0475)
- An account name with an accent (`céli`) is refused with "a-z or A-Z
  letters (no accents)", naming the spelling that would do (`celi`). No
  false "inputs/ can be read by other users" warning for a folder (such
  as inputs/slips made with mkdir) under an owner-only year or project
  folder. Outside a project, the `cd` and `-C` commands that name the
  project above are shell-quoted, so a path with a space pastes as one
  argument. (TJ-0487, TJ-0426, TJ-0571)
- The `xlsx` extra installs openpyxl only; it no longer pulls in pandas,
  which `taxjson-xlsx-to-csv` does not use. (TJ-0617)
- `tjs format` replaces two older Canadian descriptions in taxjson.toml
  (option_grant_timing_since's "SET ONCE" wording,
  corporate_distributions' README wording) with the current text instead
  of keeping them as your notes. (TJ-0595)

### Fixed: find-missing-history, opening and align

- `tjs find-missing-history` names the file and line of each REMOVE /
  STALE entry (`inputs/margin/hand.tt:1`), not missing_history.tt, and
  the checklist's missing-history step names it too. (TJ-0165)
- `--write-purchases` dates an IB Closed Lot on its settlement date
  under `tax_date = "settle"` (IB's lot date is the trade date), so a
  kept line is converted at the right day's rate. (TJ-0419)
- A short made by a trade in an old ticker after its .tt RENAME is named
  as the RENAME line's `late=` case; find-missing-history and
  `--write-missing-history` no longer suggest a purchase or an opening
  for it. (TJ-0442)
- `tjs opening ... --force` replaces the .tt as a file you keep: a
  read-only file or a link leaving the project is refused, and a link
  inside the project keeps pointing at its target, which is replaced
  with a .bak. (TJ-0586)
- `tjs align --from YEAR --write --all` commented out the `type` of an
  account only one year has, and the next run stopped. Such an account
  is listed ("[accounts] only in 2024: rrsp"), never added or removed,
  and `tjs years` counts it as a difference from the newest year ("N
  account(s)"); a taxjson.toml the config check would refuse is never
  written. (TJ-0349)
- `--write-purchases` reads the run's own pairing of transfer rows. With
  an account named, it could call a transfer-in "a move from your
  account X" that the run books as coming from outside your books, and
  it paired crypto and `transfers = true` accounts' rows, which the run
  leaves out. (TJ-0599)
- A file `tjs align --write` cannot write is named from the folder the
  command ran in (2025/ticker.map), with the fix, as format and
  format-map name theirs. (TJ-0604)
- The standalone `taxjson-missing-history BOOK --country usa
  --write-purchases FILE` (outside a project) keeps IB's Closed Lots
  date, the trade date that starts a US lot's holding period, as a US
  project does. It no longer moves the lot to its settlement date, which
  could turn a long-term gain short-term once the draft was kept.
  Outside a project, `--country` now sets the drafts' date basis to the
  country's default `tax_date`, so `--year` uses trade dates for the US
  and settlement dates for Canada. The stderr note says which basis it
  used. Canadian drafts are unchanged (TJ-0711).

### Fixed: .tt files

- A warrant's or right's exercise keeps its link to the shares in a
  `.tt` file: an ASSIGN line takes `exercise_of=SHARES`, which
  `taxjson-convert-tt` and `tjs events` write and `tjs check-tt` and
  `tjs run` read. An exported or copied exercise read back as a sale of
  the warrants at 0, a capital loss of their cost. (TJ-0377)
- `tjs events`, `divs`, `dil` and `roc` end a dividend, payment in lieu,
  tax or ADJUST line with the row's income facts (`record=`, `label=`,
  `ex=`, `dealer=`, `issuer=`, `type=`), as `taxjson-convert-tt` writes
  them, so a copied January trust distribution with a December record
  date stays in the record year. An opening balance is shown as its
  `OPENING` line, not as a `BUYSELL ... 00:00:00` purchase that read
  back without its lot date. (TJ-0390, TJ-0589)
- A stock dividend's shares stay a stock dividend in a `.tt` file:
  `taxjson-convert-tt` and `tjs events` write `type=stock_dividend`
  (with `ex=` / `record=` when known), and the reader takes it back.
  (TJ-0528)
- A `key=` token given twice on one line (`record=`, `plan=`, `type=`,
  `exercise_of=` ...) is refused, with both values named. The first
  value was kept without a word: `plan=own plan=rrsp` read as a move of
  your own. (TJ-0386)
- A contract size of a million or more, or below 0.0001, is written in
  decimals (`x1000000`, `x0.00001`), and `x1e+06`, as older releases
  wrote it, reads; it was refused. A line with a contract size of x0 is
  refused once, naming its line and what the size means. (TJ-0385,
  TJ-0207)
- An `OPENING ... cost=unknown` line keeps a `#` inside escaped double
  quotes or single quotes in its reason; it was refused as an unclosed
  quote. (TJ-0537)

### Fixed: parsers: Questrade, RBC Direct and IB

- A reinvestment reversal (Questrade CIL/REI/STK DIV, RBC Direct)
  cancels only an original of its own broker account and, at Questrade,
  its own currency. A USD reversal could cancel a CAD reinvestment, or
  one account's reversal another account's reinvestment in the same
  folder. (TJ-0517, TJ-0518)
- Questrade: the taxable-versus-registered check covers all of an
  account's exports, not each file alone, so a LIRA or TFSA export
  beside a margin export in a taxable folder is refused even in separate
  files. A lone plan whose Account Type contradicts the folder's type
  gets an ATTENTION line. (TJ-0527, TJ-0477)
- An option with an impossible expiry (February 30) or a strike the OCC
  symbol cannot hold (finer than 0.001, zero, 100000 or more) is refused
  with its file and line, instead of being booked or rounded onto
  another contract. (TJ-0519, TJ-0520)
- IB: a dividend or return of capital named by ISIN is placed on the
  listing held on its date, by a replay that applies splits and ticker
  changes; a payment before a split listing's first trade could land on
  that listing. (TJ-0521)
- RBC: the US-dollar units EXTRACT suggestion uses words that every
  US-dollar row of the fund carries, and `--suggest` no longer presents
  a narrower line as the answer. (TJ-0438)
- A row the schema check refuses from an IB, RBC Direct, Webull,
  Coinbase or Kraken export is named by its line (`ib_demo.csv line 9:
  ...`), not a masked row id. A broker file's refusal names the file
  once, and a generic mapping named after an account number is masked in
  every message. (TJ-0124, TJ-0234, TJ-0235, TJ-0236)
- Questrade, a US project: a TFSA, RESP, RDSP or FHSA export is a
  taxable account, since a US return gives these plans no treaty
  deferral (tax-logic US-BASIS-09). Beside the margin account's exports
  it is booked under `combined_broker_accounts = true` instead of
  refused; in a sheltered account's folder it gets an ATTENTION line. An
  RRSP's or RRIF's rows beside a margin account's are still refused.
  (TJ-0613)
- A warrant or right exercise with no single share leg (IB's ATTENTION
  line, RBC Direct's refusal) gives the .tt lines that book it,
  `exercise_of=` included, and says to remove the row from the export.
  (TJ-0590)
- A trade in US dollars on a Canadian market (a TSX fund's US-dollar
  unit such as QZX.U.TO) with no printed settlement date now settles on
  the next day both Canadian and US clearing settle. Before, it could
  settle on a US-only holiday (Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Memorial Day,
  Juneteenth, the Fourth of July or the Friday it is observed, US
  Thanksgiving), and its cost or proceeds was converted at that day's
  Bank of Canada rate. This applies to IB, to a blank Questrade, RBC or
  generic settle cell, to IB Closed Lots .tt drafts and to tjs
  check-dates. A printed settle date is used as printed (tax-logic
  CA-DATE-05; TJ-0705).
- A reversed reinvestment, stock dividend or cash in lieu drops out of
  both overlapping downloads even when they write its numbers
  differently (10 and -100 in one, 10.0000 and -100.00 in the other).
  One copy stayed in the books as phantom units and cost, with no
  message. (TJ-0666)

### Fixed: parsers: Webull and the generic importer

- Webull: one account's downloads pasted into one file are read download
  by download, each in its own row order (newest-first ones bottom-up),
  the same as when saved as separate files. A same-day sale and rebuy
  replayed rebuy first, which changed the cost of the shares sold.
  (TJ-0376)
- Webull: a file holding two accounts' downloads stops the run, naming
  the line, with a message to save each account's download as its own
  file. The second account's trades were booked under the first
  account's number. (TJ-0237)
- The generic importer matches `[actions]` keys ignoring case and
  surrounding spaces, as it matches row cells. Two keys alike that way
  with different values are refused (the last one won silently), and a
  key written with spaces now matches. (TJ-0382)

### Fixed: fetch, prices and exchange rates

- `tjs fetch --positions` (Questrade) wrote an empty snapshot at exit 0
  from a malformed positions response (an item without openQuantity, a
  non-number price); it refuses it and keeps the previous live-holdings
  snapshot. The snapshot gives an option the books' contract size
  (`multiplier`, or `contract_multiplier_unknown` when the books
  disagree), so a mini contract's cost is no longer read at 100 shares,
  and it reads Questrade's class-share option symbols such as
  SYN.B20Jan26C88.00. (TJ-0513, TJ-0514, TJ-0515)
- The overlap warning of `tjs fetch` (Questrade) checks a manual export
  saved as questrade_YYYY.csv: only rows the fetch wrote itself (Account
  Type API) are left out, and `--trim-overlap` keeps them. (TJ-0516)
- The price cache: a day's-close entry whose unit taxjson cannot read
  (such as "USd") was served in the listing's currency; it is a miss and
  is looked up again. A cached current quote dated after today, beyond
  one day of clock skew, is not used, and the warning names the cache
  file (an entry dated 2099 was shown as the current price). A boolean
  from a price source or the cache is not a price: JSON true was quoted
  and cached at 1. (TJ-0575, TJ-0576, TJ-0577)
- Exchange rates: two runs downloading rates at the same time keep each
  other's series in ~/.currency_price_cache.json; the later save dropped
  the other's new rates. A date no calendar has (2025-02-30) stopped the
  rates stage with "ValueError: day is out of range for month": in the
  rate cache it is dropped and reported as damage, and as `--start` or
  `--end` it is a usage error. Fetching rates from Yahoo no longer
  prints yfinance's own unlabelled lines. (TJ-0583, TJ-0584, TJ-0242)
- `tjs fetch --positions` (Questrade): a live option the books do not
  hold yet takes the contract size Questrade's symbol lookup states; a
  mini contract was costed at 100 shares. When the lookup gives none,
  the snapshot and a note say the standard 100 is assumed. (TJ-0614)
- Two runs at once, one online and one offline (TAXJSON_OFFLINE), that
  both found the same damaged rate in the shared FX rate cache: the rate
  the online run downloaded again stays covered whichever saves second,
  so offline runs use it instead of having no rate for that day (or an
  earlier day's rate). A cleanup now uncovers a day only while the cache
  still holds the damaged value (TJ-0706).
- tjs fetch --positions (Questrade): Questrade gives the shares a
  contract delivers. For an option the books do not hold yet, that
  number is no longer taken as the contract size of a contract adjusted
  by a corporate action (root SYN1 on SYN). Its cost is now unknown
  (contract_multiplier_unknown) instead of a tenth of the premium paid
  after a 1-for-10 reverse split. A mini contract whose root is its
  underlying's symbol still takes its stated size. (TJ-0670)

### Fixed: redact

- `tjs redact` reads each CSV record whole: an account number after a
  quoted cell with a line break is replaced, a two-line alias is blanked
  whole, and a record whose quotes never close is listed for review.
  (TJ-0414)
- A data row is never read as a column header: a row with a holder word
  in its Description (WIRE TO BENEFICIARY ...), or in a comma-separated
  file a row of text only, kept its name, blanked later Description
  cells or had the copy refused. A short account id from taxjson.toml
  (`query_id = "2025"`) is replaced only in its own key's value, so the
  copy's year stays as it is. (TJ-0479, TJ-0569, TJ-0579)
- A year folder's copy carries the close-year record its estimate reads,
  as prior/<name>, and its `prior_year_record` names it. A taxjson.toml
  or ticker.map that links to a file inside the project is copied; a
  link pointing elsewhere is named, and the copy is not called runnable
  without a taxjson.toml. (TJ-0581, TJ-0580)
- `tjs -C inputs_redact redact --check` reads every file of a copy laid
  out as a project (settings files, holdings/ and prior/ too) and names
  the work/ and reports/ a run of the copy wrote, exiting 1. The closing
  line says to delete them before sharing, and its `taxjson -C <copy>
  run` hint is shell-quoted. (TJ-0480, TJ-0484, TJ-0486)
- An e-mail address in an export's file or folder name is replaced in
  the copy, and a file or folder name that reads like a person's is
  listed to rename by hand. (TJ-0481)
- A line such as `Name,Jane,Sample` (a label word, then a name split
  over cells) is an identity line, and the name is redacted. It was
  taken for the export's column header and kept, and an address line
  after it was kept too. (TJ-0608)
- `tjs redact` in a year folder: the close-year record the copy carries
  as `prior/<year>.json` no longer keeps a folder path of this computer,
  such as the shared `inputs_dir` its year was frozen from, a
  carry-forward's source or the `--filed-dispositions` file, where these
  held the home folder or a person's name. Each becomes `<redacted
  path>` and is counted as a folder path of this computer, and `tjs -C
  <copy> redact --check` names one left in a copy, with its line (exit
  1). The copy's estimate still carries the loss in (TJ-0700).

### Fixed: messages

- A write refused in a read-only folder (checklist.json and others)
  names the folder and the `chmod u+w` to run, and a read-only file's
  chmod names its path from where the command was run. (TJ-0218,
  TJ-0219)
- In a year folder, a file no broker matches in the shared exports is
  named ../inputs/<account>/<file>, and the elections manifest is named
  as `tjs elect` names it, not by its absolute path. (TJ-0253, TJ-0216)
- A command function called in-process (tests, a GUI) names its own
  command in its messages, not the one an earlier call left set. `tjs
  --di DIR ...` (any abbreviation of `--dir` argparse accepts, or
  `--di=DIR`) reads the project in DIR when deciding whether a chained
  word is an account (`events sum`) and for the help page, as `-C DIR`
  does. (TJ-0354, TJ-0553)
- The corp-actions stage's note in
  work/<account>_<broker>_corp.json.diag names the pending elections
  file work/<account>_pending_elections.json, not its absolute path (the
  stage's new `--pending-json-shown` flag). (TJ-0602)
- `tjs amt` and `tjs instalments`: when the estimate they build on
  fails, the relayed error is one Error with the estimate's reason under
  it (a second "Error: taxjson estimate: ..." showed inside the first),
  and it keeps the line that names the cause: with a long project path
  only the hint was shown. A very long line keeps both ends. close-year,
  watch and wash-sales relay a child's error the same way. (TJ-0633,
  TJ-0625)
- A damaged work/ gains file is named once, as work/<file> with its
  reason, no longer a second time by its absolute path. `tjs sum`,
  `estimate` and `plot-tax` exit 2 for it, an input that cannot be read,
  and `tjs amt` and `tjs instalments` keep the estimate's exit 2
  (TJ-0641).

### Fixed: speed

- A US project's run slowed with the square of one security's trades.
  The wash-sale check finds each loss's replacements in an index by
  trade date, row and lot instead of walking every purchase and short
  sale (8,000 rows of one symbol: `tjs run` 72 s -> 10 s; 16,000 rows:
  271 s -> 23 s). No figure changes. (TJ-0238)
- `tjs wash-radar` (and buy-check, sell-check, watch and the run's radar
  reports) reads only the purchases in each loss's window instead of
  every purchase of the security (32,000 rows over 16 years: 8.6 s ->
  3.0 s). No line changes. (TJ-0239)
- Reading a work/ JSON file skips the comment-stripping pass when the
  file has no comment, which cost about ten times the parse (an
  8,000-row run: 13.6 s -> 10.1 s with the radar change). Hand-commented
  files read as before. (TJ-0240)

### Changed: tax-logic

- New rules: CA-RPT-14 (a T1135 row's INCOME: the property's dividends
  and payments in lieu, dated as the return dates them, and the interest
  the books tie to it), US-STKDIV-05 (shares entitled to a stock
  dividend but sold before its pay date keep their part of the new
  shares) and US-EST-CEILING (the tax on long-term gains and qualified
  dividends is at most the tax on all of the taxable income at the
  ordinary rates). (TJ-0504, TJ-0488, TJ-0498, TJ-0509)
- Canada, the estimate and T1135: CA-EST-FTC states the T2209 / T2036
  limits and that a spin-off's deemed dividend takes no assumed
  withholding; CA-EST-AMT the s.127.54 special foreign tax credit and
  the incremental top-up. CA-RPT-02 and CA-RPT-18 add a Canadian
  issuer's shares held with a custodian outside Canada (category 6, at
  the account's share of the pooled ACB) and a Canadian listing with
  another country's ISIN; CA-RPT-12 gives a futures contract the
  superficial loss added to it as its cost amount. (TJ-0367, TJ-0368,
  TJ-0422, TJ-0489, TJ-0369, TJ-0455, TJ-0505)
- Moves: CA-ACB-OWN-MOVE covers coins moved between your taxable crypto
  accounts; CA-ACB-TRANSFER-BV, US-BASIS-TRANSFER-BV and US-BASIS-05 say
  that a leg an in-kind move pairs is never a move of your own, that the
  listings the run joins by their transfer journal count as one
  security, and that US lots move by the one pairing; CA-INKIND-01 and
  US-INKIND-01 list legs 11 to 45 days apart NOT booked; CA-CORP-13
  weighs a merger by the holdings after a move of your own. (TJ-0281,
  TJ-0230, TJ-0440, TJ-0269, TJ-0437, TJ-0280)
- US: US-WASH-18 puts broad-based index options with the §1256 contracts
  outside the wash-sale rule; US-WASH-12 sizes the call flag on the loss
  shares no purchase replaced; US-WASH-22 keeps a basis add the filed
  lock already has; US-STKDIV-01 and -03 grow a purchase's wash-sale
  capacity by its stock dividend; US-RPT-13 and CA-RPT-07 read the
  carried denials on the project's tax_date; US-CARRY-01, -03, -04 and
  US-EST-CARRY-TI take `[carryover] claimed` as the deduction used;
  US-RPT-06 records the Dec 31 lots that handoff compares. (TJ-0506,
  TJ-0467, TJ-0463, TJ-0492, TJ-0343, TJ-0464, TJ-0554)
- Planning and views: CA-PLAN-01, CA-PLAN-05, US-PLAN-01 and US-PLAN-02
  state settlement dating, both listings' calendars and a buy's amount
  per unit; CA-PLAN-07 and US-PLAN-08 the option yield's currency;
  CA-RPT-16 and US-RPT-12 the trade statistics' put premium and
  unknown-cost sales. (TJ-0243, TJ-0446, TJ-0559, TJ-0560, TJ-0543,
  TJ-0546, TJ-0545)
- Also reworded: CA-CARRY-04 (a year's own claimed entry), CA-OPT-07
  (close timing after a grant-timing lock), CA-SLIP-03 (a T3's box 42
  spread), CA-SCAN-01 (TFSA-US-DIV by domicile), CA-CORP-06 (the s.86.1
  election for a foreign parent only), CA-CRYPTO-08 (self sends stay in
  the pool), CA-FX-07 and US-FX-03 (a conversion's commission; in-kind
  moves move no cash), CA-INC-STAKING and US-INC-STAKING (a fiat
  reward's income in its own currency), CA-DATE-14 and US-DATE-13
  (downloads pasted into one file), CA-ACB-15 (an IB lot drafted on its
  settlement date) and CA-ACB-RENAME / US-BASIS-RENAME (a short after a
  rename). CA-CTRY-02 and US-CTRY-02 list `custodian_country` as
  Canada-only and the gains engine's new `--lots-at` and
  `--locked-record` flags as US-only. (TJ-0223, TJ-0396, TJ-0420,
  TJ-0562, TJ-0441, TJ-0501, TJ-0456, TJ-0494, TJ-0378, TJ-0379,
  TJ-0376, TJ-0419, TJ-0442)
- New rules: CA-RPT-20 (an account's cash held outside Canada is a
  category 1 row at its cost day by day, on the project's tax_date
  basis), US-BASIS-09 (a Canadian TFSA, RESP, RDSP or FHSA is taxable
  for a US filer; the treaty defers an RRSP or RRIF) and US-FUT-03 (the
  §1256 60/40 split). CA-RPT-02, CA-RPT-14, CA-RPT-15 and CA-RPT-18 add
  the cash rows, their interest income and category 1; CA-FX-07 says an
  opening balance moves no cash and where a conversion's commission in a
  foreign currency goes. (TJ-0454, TJ-0609, TJ-0627, TJ-0628, TJ-0613,
  TJ-0466, TJ-0621, TJ-0622)
- The minimum tax and the foreign tax credit: CA-EST-FTC works the
  provincial credit as form T2036 does in a minimum-tax year and names
  the foreign tax no credit takes as possibly deductible; CA-EST-AMT
  gives Alberta's and British Columbia's minimum tax the base their
  forms use; CA-AMT-02 and CA-AMT-07 make the carryover the s.120.2(3)
  additional tax. US: US-FUT-02 leaves year-end marking and the §1212(c)
  carryback by hand, and US-OPT-04 and US-RPT-07 split the §1256 P/L
  60/40. (TJ-0591, TJ-0592, TJ-0626, TJ-0466)

### Fixed: developer tools and the docs

- `scripts/land.sh` uses GitHub's auto-merge only when main's rules
  require an up-to-date branch; otherwise it merges the pull request
  itself once every check has passed. When main moved and the landed
  commits do not sit on the base they were gated on, it says so.
  (TJ-0214)
- `scripts/release.sh --prepare` refuses a version commit that has
  commits on top of it, because GitHub CI runs on the head of a push
  only and the cut would find no run; after a failed check it advises
  taking the version commit back before a fix. (TJ-0213)
- The gate's suite and its no-extras stage hide the taxjson-fetch
  plugin, as GitHub's jobs do (the sitecustomize that hides the extras
  and the plugin is `scripts/hide_optional.py`), and the no-extras stage
  runs the test modules that use it. The suite refuses what CI's Python
  3.10 job would: a child Python started with `-P` (or a newer `-X`
  option) outside `python_module_argv`, and an `import tomllib` without
  its fallback; CONTRIBUTING.md gives the 3.10 run for the rest.
  (TJ-0267, TJ-0290, TJ-0594)
- `scripts/check-pii.sh --help` prints its usage, and an unknown option
  is refused. An empty folder no longer reports the figure-list guard as
  DISABLED, and file-name and figure-list hits show their path as every
  other hit does, with only an id-shaped part masked. (TJ-0265, TJ-0215)
- `scripts/ci.sh --help` and CONTRIBUTING.md name every stage of the
  default gate. The developer docs' line-count ranges are checked for
  each file they name, and `taxjson_run.py` is given as about 34k lines.
  (TJ-0227, TJ-0228)
- Tidying: test_edge_cases starts its child Python through
  `python_module_argv`, three modules drop unused imports, and the
  crypto-sends troubleshooting heading quotes the checklist's `!` lines
  as they read now. (TJ-0344, TJ-0346, TJ-0206)
- taxjson builds every child Python through `python_module_argv`, so the
  folder it runs in is never on `sys.path`: the pipeline stages and the
  commands that relay another command's `--json` too (`run_cmd` still
  runs them in process). A source scan in the tests fails on any other
  Python launch in the package. (TJ-0632)
- `scripts/dev-setup.sh` removes the `*.egg-info` folders editable
  builds leave in `src/` and `packages/*/src/`, and checks the venv's
  taxjson and taxjson-fetch versions against the code with the new
  `scripts/editable_check.py`; `scripts/release.sh` reinstalls the fetch
  plugin with the core after a version bump. `scripts/lock_deps.py
  --coverage` lists the known Intel-macOS gap of the optional `all` and
  `generate-parser` locks (cryptography has no wheel there) as accepted,
  with its reason (`ACCEPTED_GAPS`); any other gap is still reported.
  (TJ-0636, TJ-0637)
- Tests: a phrase looked for in `tjs` output (`tj()`, the style
  projects' `Project.run`) is found across a line break, so a temp
  path's length no longer decides where it wraps. Tests that plant
  work/to_base.csv put the same rates in the HOME's currency cache
  (`tests/_planted_rates.py`), so a run that rebuilds the file keeps
  them, and the suite's shared HOME is restored after each test. A new
  test pins the split's year-end share on a trade-date project, already
  right. (TJ-0625, TJ-0606, TJ-0635, TJ-0607)
- The CHANGELOG's v0.24.1 to v0.30.1 sections and the troubleshooting
  playbook cite the earlier repository's numbers as "audit N", so GitHub
  no longer links them to unrelated issues. (TJ-0172)
- The gate (`scripts/ci.sh`) and CI's lint job now refuse an unused
  import (ruff F401) and also lint `scripts/`; a test keeps the two lint
  lines equal. The 169 unused imports left in src, tests and scripts are
  gone, and each import kept on purpose (a re-export, a side effect, an
  availability check) says why on its `# noqa: F401` line. (TJ-0593)

## v0.37.0 (2026-10-27)

### Fixed: transfers

- A sheltered account's move between brokers was refused when a trade
  of the security sat between its legs' dates (the arrival posted after
  a buy at the new broker, or the old broker dated its transfer-out
  later), and so was a listing journal (IB InterDepot) with a move a
  few weeks later and a sale between them. The refused rows were booked
  as sales and purchases at the rows' values: gains that never
  happened, and the cost restarted at the arrival's price (often 0) in
  the books, `reports/<account>.sum` and the holdings export. A
  sheltered account's own books now net a move whatever trades of the
  account sit inside it (a split still blocks). In every account a
  trade or a split between two transfer rows separates two moves, each
  netted on its own, so a taxable account with a journal and a move
  around a sale no longer stops. (TJ-0360)

### Fixed: holdings

- `reports/<account>_holdings.toml` costs a holding journaled from one
  listing to the other (a TSX line to its US line, a Norbert's gambit)
  as the books do. The native-currency books behind it moved a
  journal's units after the gains, so a sale of the new listing after
  the journal was booked against nothing and the export's cost mixed
  the old listing's cost with the sale's proceeds (`mixed_currency`, a
  wrong `base_total_cost`); an account with `transfers = true` booked
  the two legs as a sale and a purchase at their market value. The run
  now books each journal in the native books on its date: its units
  move with their cost, restated in the new listing's currency at the
  day's rate. (TJ-0361, TJ-0363)

### Added: the lock records which taxjson closed it

- `tjs close-year` records in `filed/<year>.json` which taxjson computed
  the figures (`taxjson`: the version and, for a git install, the
  commit, the release tag and whether a file was modified). When
  `tjs check-filed` finds a drift it names it: the same taxjson (the
  change is in the inputs or the settings) or another (the releases
  between them say what each moved). A lock closed before this release
  names none. (TJ-0341)

### Added: T1135 categories

- `tjs t1135` shows each property's T1135 category (CAT, the form's 1 to
  6): 6 for an option, a futures contract or crypto, 2 for any other
  listed security. Units or a fund the interlisted master knows are left
  for you to set and named. A ticker.map line sets a category: `T1135
  SYMBOL COUNTRY CATEGORY` (the category is optional). `--json` adds
  `category` and `category_from` to each property and
  `category_review_symbols`. (TJ-0291)

### Fixed: t1135

- `tjs t1135` left out a foreign holding held at a zero cost (free
  shares): it is a property row now, at 0.00. A position opened at an
  unknown cost and sold during the year lost its "unknown ACB" flag with
  the sale, so its maximum cost read as known; it keeps the flag for the
  year. (TJ-0292)
- `tjs t1135` listed a written option closed during the year (or a
  covered short sale) as a property row at 0.00 cost with its gain. A
  position held only short is an obligation, not property held: it is
  named in a `! ` line, not listed, and its gain is no longer in the
  per-country totals. `--json` adds `short_only_symbols`. (TJ-0295)

### Fixed: year end: carryover, close-year, check-filed and edge-cases

- US `tjs carryover`: a wash-sale loss whose replacement another account
  bought and sold in a filed (locked) year is now in the loss's year, as
  `tjs run` books it; it was in no year, and the carryover after it was
  too low. (TJ-0296)
- US `tjs carryover`: a crypto account's sales with an unknown cost are
  named in the warning, with their years, and in `--json`
  (`excluded_unknown_cost`, `incomplete_years`, a row's `incomplete`);
  `first_transaction_year` counts crypto rows. They used to vanish
  without a word. (TJ-0323)
- US `tjs close-year`: a crypto account's year-end record is computed
  without the wash-sale rule, as the run computes it, so the next year's
  `tjs handoff` no longer flags a cost difference after a crypto loss
  and repurchase. (TJ-0297)
- Canada `tjs close-year`: a symbol's Dec 31 `deferred` in the record is
  what is left of each superficial-loss addition after the sales before
  Dec 31, not their sum; the recorded cost is unchanged. (TJ-0285)
- `tjs close-year --filed-dispositions` refuses a row dated in another
  year than the one being closed, naming its line, before anything is
  written; `--force` refuses to keep such a row from the lock it
  replaces. (TJ-0298)
- `tjs check-filed`, `tjs years` and the next year's lock readers treat
  a lock whose `return_row` is not a table of finite numbers as damaged;
  check-filed's OK line says the RETURN row is not recomputed. (TJ-0274)
- `tjs edge-cases` in a US project listed the disallowed losses carried
  into the next year from the books' final lots ("held at the end of the
  books, which may be after 2025"): a sale in the next year shrank or
  emptied the list, a purchase added to it, and a January loss on shares
  bought in December showed as carried from the year. They now come from
  the US engine's lots at the end of Dec 31 of the project year (the
  gains files' new `inventory_year_end`, read on trade dates; a
  `tax_date = "settle"` project is told so), as Canada's pools have
  since v0.36.1, so later trades change nothing. Nothing filed changes.
  Re-run `tjs run` once. (TJ-0284)

### Fixed: migrate, missing history, opening, align and fetch

- `tjs migrate` in a multi-year project plans every phase before the
  first one writes. An old file it cannot convert (a malformed
  `amt_carryover.txt`, a `missing_history.json` whose books are not
  built) now stops it with nothing changed. Before, it had already made
  the year folders' tobase.map copies one shared file and still said
  "Nothing was changed." A refusal after an earlier phase wrote ends
  with "Done before it, and kept: …". (TJ-0300)
- `tjs find-missing-history --write-missing-history` dates sales by the
  project's `tax_date`. In a trade-dated Canadian project, or a
  settle-dated US one, a sale traded on Dec 31 and settling in January,
  which the report lists under AFFECTS, was filtered out and no line was
  written. (TJ-0316)
- `tjs opening ACCOUNT FILE --date 2025-1-1` is refused ("is not a
  YYYY-MM-DD date", "Write it 2025-01-01"). Before, it wrote
  `opening_2025-1-1.tt`, which the next `tjs run` refused. Each OPENING
  line is now read back as the run reads it before the file is written.
  (TJ-0317)
- `tjs align --from YEAR --write --all --json` prints one JSON result
  once the files are written: the differences, plus `written`, `files`,
  `map_lines_added`, `map_lines_skipped`, `keys_set`,
  `keys_not_changed`, `filed_year` and `warnings`. Before, it printed
  prose. `--write --json` without `--all` is refused (exit 2). (TJ-0318)
- `tjs fetch --list` runs in a project that still has an old per-purpose
  file such as `yf_ticker.map`, as it does in any folder; `tjs check-tt
  FILE.tt` too. (TJ-0217)
- `tjs promote` (its help and docs/commands.md) says it pushes a
  `channels-<UTC time>` fast-lane tag, with no new release tag and no
  rebuild. (TJ-0337)

### Fixed: transfers, renames, check-dates, journals, check-tt and the checklist

- `tjs transfers`: a taxable transfer-in reads "own move" only when the
  pairing matched it with a transfer-out of yours. When a converted .tt
  file in work/ cannot be read, a warning names it, and each such
  arrival reads UNCLASSIFIED (a `! N transfer-in(s) UNCLASSIFIED` line),
  not "own move". (TJ-0308)
- `tjs renames` in a US project shows the FIFO basis of the lots a
  rename carries, as the books do, not the average cost. Canada's
  average cost is unchanged. (TJ-0309)
- `tjs check-dates`: a parsed source that `work/<account>_sources.list`
  names but work/ lacks is an ERROR (`missing`, exit 1, "N parsed
  source(s) not checked: re-run `taxjson run`"), not 0 rows checked
  clean. An unreadable source is counted the same way, not as a wrong
  date. (TJ-0319)
- `tjs renames` with no books refuses ("run `taxjson run` first", exit
  1), like `tjs splits` and `tjs spinoffs`. (TJ-0319)
- `tjs splits`, `tjs spinoffs` and `tjs renames` refuse a damaged book
  in work/ (a row that is not a JSON object, or a `transactions` that is
  not a list), naming the file and the row; a valid empty book is still
  clean. (TJ-0320)
- `tjs journals` refuses a `work/cross_listings.state` whose record
  lists or records are damaged, naming the record, instead of reading it
  as no journals pending. (TJ-0321)
- `tjs check-tt` reports two known-cost OPENING snapshots of one symbol
  with two dates as an ERROR of the second line, naming the other, as
  `tjs run` refuses them; in a project and for named files. (TJ-0322)
- `tjs checklist`: the format step reads ticker.map with its tobase.map,
  as the run does. A line the run refuses needs attention, with the
  count, the files and the first line. The checks no longer repeat the
  loader's "Warning: ticker.map problem:" lines. (TJ-0250, TJ-0112)

### Fixed: slip-audit, t1135 and sanity

- `tjs slip-audit`: what it cannot compare makes the audit incomplete:
  status `incomplete`, the new `--json` key `not_compared`, exit 1, no
  "Every slip agrees", and the checklist's `t5-t3` step blocked or
  needing attention, never done. This covers an account with inputs and
  no readable books, an IB dividends report no account's books carry, an
  IB component taxjson does not know, and a `broker_key` no broker
  account matches. A second copy of a report, a pay-dated ROC line and a
  legacy `broker_key` stay notices. (TJ-0305)
- `tjs t1135`: an account whose books are in work/ without its gains
  file is refused with an Error naming it; its income and gain(loss)
  columns used to read 0 at exit 0. (TJ-0306)
- `tjs sanity` (no arguments): an account whose gains file cannot be
  read, or that has inputs and no gains file, stops the check with an
  Error instead of dropping out of the coverage; `--json` used to say
  `clean` and `complete` over it. (TJ-0307)
- `taxjson-reconcile-slips`: a `--gains` file whose dispositions or
  `metadata.target_currency` are in another currency than the country's
  is refused (exit 2); USD gains used to reconcile OK against CAD slips
  with the same numbers. (TJ-0325)

### Fixed: planning views and redact

- `tjs wash-radar`, `watch`, `rebuy`, `buy-check` and `sell-check`
  printed a sentence instead of JSON under `--json` in a project the
  wash rule does not reach (a US project whose taxable accounts are all
  crypto, or sheltered accounts only). Each now prints its usual
  document with nothing in it and `not_applicable` giving the reason,
  exit 0; `wash-radar ACCOUNT --json` on a US crypto account too.
  (TJ-0330)
- `tjs watch` with a book missing from `work/` (`sheltered_base.json`,
  or a taxable account's `<account>_base.json`) reported "LOCKED ->
  CLEAR — safe to sell at a loss" and saved that as its baseline. It now
  compares nothing, keeps the baseline and says so in a warning;
  `--json` adds `incomplete`. (TJ-0303)
- `tjs buy-check`, `sell-check` and `rebuy` skipped a ticker.map or
  tobase.map line they could not parse and answered from the rest: a
  broken `GLOBAL OLD NEW` line turned an UNSAFE buy into SAFE. They now
  refuse the map as `tjs run` does, naming each line, exit 2. (TJ-0304)
- `tjs redact` could give two accounts one placeholder, or swap them,
  when the input held an id already shaped like one (`99900001`,
  `U9990001`), within a file or across a project copy. A placeholder is
  now never another id of what is copied, and ids are replaced in one
  pass. (TJ-0249)
- `tjs redact` and `--check` list a description that starts with a bare
  FROM or TO and a name (`FROM SAM SAMPLE`) for review; it was neither
  replaced nor listed. (TJ-0248)

### Fixed: plot-tax, stats, fees and the time windows

- `tjs plot-tax` (Canada) credited 15% foreign withholding on every run,
  while `tjs estimate` credits the TAX rows the books record, so its
  months and year differed from the estimate. It now reads the same
  withholding: each month the TAX rows dated by its end (a withholding
  posted after its dividend lowers that later month), and the 15%
  assumption only for an account whose books record none in the year.
  (TJ-0299)
- US `tjs stats` / `tjs win-rates` counted a sale that took several FIFO
  lots as one trade per lot (a sale of a winning and a losing lot: 2
  trades, 1 win, 1 loss). A closed trade is now a closing disposition,
  its lots' P/L added; the denied and unknown-cost counts are
  dispositions too. NET_P/L is unchanged. (TJ-0327)
- `tjs fees` dropped every fee under half a cent before adding the
  total: three 0.004 commissions said "No fees incurred". Every fee is
  now in TOTAL FEES, summed before rounding; one under half a cent is
  not listed as a row, and the count line (`--json`:
  `unlisted_small_fees`) says how many. (TJ-0328)
- `30d` / `6w` / `3m` / `1y` / `mtd` / `ytd` windows included rows dated
  after today (a trade entered ahead) in every windowed view (`events`,
  `trades`, `fees`, the `-sum` roll-ups, `stats`, `win-rates`,
  `winners`, `gains` …) and in `fees-sum`. They now end today; `all`, a
  year and `tax_year` are unchanged. `taxjson-fees-sum` takes `--until`,
  and its `--json` meta has `until`. (TJ-0329)
### Fixed: audit

- `tjs audit`: the tie-out compares each sale's quantity, proceeds,
  cost, gain, disallowed amounts, symbol, dates, account, direction and
  term, each lot's acquired date and share, and the replacement lots
  with the saved gains file; only the gain and the disallowed amount
  were compared. An unknown-cost sale is compared with its MANUAL
  REPORTING REQUIRED row. `--json`: `tie_out.mismatched`. (TJ-0332)
- `tjs audit`: a sale already in the base currency has its amount
  compared with its parsed row (it was marked native, unchecked). The
  audited securities' buys, earlier sales and the replacements the sales
  name are traced too: the footer's `pool trades` line, `--json`
  `pool_trades`. The footer's `fx cross-check` line is now `sale
  amounts`, and a new `not traced` line and `--json` `scope` say what is
  not checked. (TJ-0333)
- `tjs audit` (crypto): one leg of a coin-for-coin trade that the price
  stage valued ties against that priced row; it failed "FX cross-check
  FAILED" on correct books. (found while fixing TJ-0333)
- `tjs audit` groups the accounts as the run did. A US project's crypto
  accounts with a move between them are audited as one blend, so the
  move keeps its basis. A pending election in any account holds back
  every pooled group, crypto included. (TJ-0311, TJ-0314)
- `tjs audit SYMBOL` / `--id` / `--date` / `--account`: a filtered audit
  still finds a saved sale missing from the books, or one the books do
  not produce, within the filter's scope; it passed at exit 0. (TJ-0301)
- `tjs audit` (US): a sale drawing both purchased lots and lots with no
  purchase in your files is two events: the computed part ties to the
  saved gain and the rest to MANUAL REPORTING REQUIRED. Correct books no
  longer fail. (TJ-0310)
- `tjs audit` (US, a filed year locked): a wash-sale basis add to a
  replacement sold in a filed year is booked in the loss's year, as the
  run books it; the saved row is no longer called fabricated. (TJ-0313)
- `tjs audit`: a futures close is FX-checked against its own account's
  fills, so a contract traded in two taxable accounts no longer fails
  "FX cross-check FAILED" on correct books. (TJ-0312)
- `tjs audit --json`: in a project with several books, `total_gain`
  leaves out the unknown-cost (manual) sales as the text does, with new
  `manual_reporting` totals. `failed` is true whenever the exit status
  is 1, with new `not_audited` and `coverage_failures` for an account
  not audited. (TJ-0302, TJ-0315)
- `tjs audit --summary` and `--no-trace` no longer compute pool traces,
  and the event blocks share one pool history: the time and memory no
  longer grow with the square of a symbol's sales. `--json --no-trace`
  events carry an empty `trace`. (TJ-0334)
- `tjs audit`'s `--default-rate` help no longer describes a 1.35 USD→CAD
  fallback: there is no built-in rate, and a row with no rate fails its
  FX check. (TJ-0335)
### Changed: tax-logic

- `tjs tax-logic` prints each rule as its first sentence, with its other
  sentences (and a long sentence's clauses, at its semicolons) as items
  under it, instead of one paragraph per rule; the tax tables list one
  year per item. `--json` and the rule ids (`--ids`) are unchanged.

### Added: crypto holdings

- `tjs run` writes `reports/<account>_holdings.toml` for a crypto account
  too (before, every account had one but the crypto ones): the coins from
  the account's own books, cost in the base currency, `asset_type =
  "crypto"`, quantities without float noise.

### Added: staking reports

- `tjs staking` explains individual crypto rewards and `tjs staking-sum`
  totals them by exchange and coin: value before commission, commission,
  recorded income, and evidence coverage. `--details` shows coin quantities,
  valuation, FX, source evidence and acquisition cost; `--json` exposes the
  full report. Coinbase and Kraken imports preserve reward facts so a
  withheld commission is visible without deducting it again. Older books
  show unknown commission evidence until rebuilt. Tax calculations are
  unchanged; `tax-logic` explicitly describes their staking assumptions.


## v0.36.1 (2026-10-26)

### Fixed: edge-cases

- `tjs edge-cases` showed the denied losses "still held at the end of <year>" from the books' final positions, after every later trade: a sale in the next year shrank them, a full sale dropped the holding, a purchase added to it. In Canada they now come from the engine's pools at the end of Dec 31 (the gains files' new `inventory_year_end`, split per account like the inventory), so later trades change nothing; a gains file from before, or a US project, says its figure is at the end of the books (`--json` `as_of`). Re-run `tjs run` once. (TJ-0282)
- `tjs edge-cases` explained every Canadian loss across Dec 31 that the engine denied nothing of as "the replacement was not still held on day 30, or it was sold before the window closed", unchecked. It now gives the reason the books show: a written option's exempt buy-back loss (`option_buyback_loss_superficial = false`), a `.tt` ALLOWLOSS filing position, an in-kind contribution (denied by s.40(2)(g)(iv) instead), or no units held at the end of day 30, counted; otherwise "no denial applied by the engine" (`--json` `allowed_by`). (TJ-0283)

## v0.36.0 (2026-10-26)

### Added: transfers

- A `.tt` `NOTOWN` line undoes a pairing that is not one move of your own. An unrelated transfer-out and transfer-in of the same stock and quantity in two of your taxable accounts (within 10 days, or 11 to 45 days apart when nothing else could pair with either) were paired as one move: the transfer-in took the departure's ACB (US: its lots and purchase dates), and nothing let you undo it. `NOTOWN <date> <symbol> <qty> <from-account> <from-date>` in the receiving account's folder undoes that one pairing and never makes one: the transfer-in is booked as one from outside your books, the transfer-out as an ordinary one. The slow pairing's `Own-account move` Info line prints the line to add (`tjs run --details`), a line that undoes no pairing is a Warning naming it, and `tjs check-tt` reads the keyword. The 45-day bound is unchanged, and nothing changes without the line. (TJ-0075)

### Fixed: moves between your own accounts

- Canada: a move of shares between two of your own taxable accounts left the receiving account short in `tjs list` ("missing history?"), `tjs sanity`, `tjs find-missing-history` ("fix before filing" for a correct sale) and the checklist, and following that advice took the sale off Schedule 3. Each account's books now carry the move, so the receiving account holds the shares. The pooled ACB and every Schedule 3 figure are unchanged; the per-account baselines (`<account>.sum`, holdings) move the units. (TJ-0093)
- A move between your own accounts no longer hides the export-coverage Warning for the sending account's export (it was hidden in a US project), and a sale on the day the shares arrive is no longer read as missing history. (TJ-0093)

### Fixed: carryover, close-year and years

- `tjs carryover` (Canada) showed the project year's NET GAIN(LOSS) as the books' unrounded total, a cent or two off the RETURN row of `tjs sum`, and in a loss year a carryforward a cent off what `tjs estimate` and `tjs close-year` carry forward. The year's net is now the RETURN row (`--json`: `net_source`, and the books' total as `engine_net_gain`), and an earlier year's lock gives the RETURN row close-year recorded. `tjs handoff`'s carry-back moves by the same cents. (TJ-0208)
- close-year's CLOSED block showed Income as the lock's total, a cent off `tjs sum`'s DIVIDEND subtotal; it, and `tjs years --json`'s `totals.income`, now show income as `sum`'s SUBTOTAL adds it. The lock is unchanged. (TJ-0212)
- A filed year whose `filed/<year>.json` was deleted, while its taxjson.toml still carries close-year's freeze note, was taken as never closed, and `tjs years` offered `tjs migrate`, which pointed the year back at the shared exports. It now stays frozen, as with a damaged lock: `tjs years` shows `lock missing` and says to restore the lock (from git or a backup) or run `close-year` again, `tjs migrate` leaves it alone, `tjs check-filed` and `tjs run` warn (check-filed exits 1), the checklist's lock steps are blocked, and `align --write` warns as in a filed year. `tjs new-year` from such a year, or one with a damaged lock, no longer copies the freeze note into the new year. (TJ-0263)

### Changed: sum, estimate and div-estimate

- `tjs sum` says above the RETURN row, when they differ, that SUBTOTAL adds the account rows and RETURN each sale's cents; only `--details` explained the cent or two between them. (TJ-0209)
- `tjs estimate --json` (Canada) adds `losses_carried_back` and `losses_carried_forward`, the two figures the console prints in a year whose loss `[carryover] claimed` carries back (T1A); `losses_unused` keeps its value, the loss before the carry-back. (TJ-0226)
- `tjs div-estimate` warns when a dividend is paid while the books show that account short in that security: a short position is charged a dividend, not paid one, so the books likely miss a purchase or a transfer in. One warning per account and security, naming `tjs find-missing-history`; the position's flags (`--details`, `--json` `flags`) carry the same note. The payment still counts in the estimate. (TJ-0073)

### Fixed: init and the run's reports

- `tjs init --force` replaced a taxjson.toml you made read-only without a word. It now refuses as the other writers do ("the file is read-only", `chmod u+w` to allow it, exit 2), and nothing is written. (TJ-0220)
- A blended account's `<account>_wash.sum` DIAGNOSTICS showed a message about another account's file as if it were its own. Such a message now starts with that account's name (`[margin] `); messages about the whole blend are unchanged, and nothing is left out. (TJ-0252)

### Fixed: check-tt, `.tt` files and the checklist

- `tjs check-tt` said "Every line parses." for a `TRANSFER` or `ACQUIRED` line in a taxable account, and for a `SPLIT` ratio of 0 or below, all of which stop `tjs run`. Each is now an error naming its line and the fix. A zero-net pair, or a line an `OPENING` snapshot replaces, is still fine. A taxable account with `transfers = true` gets a warning, since an export's TRANSFER row may cancel the line. The run's own refusal of a bad SPLIT ratio now names the `.tt` line instead of a work file. (TJ-0006)
- `tjs check-tt FILE.tt` checked the file's lines one by one only. A symbol opened twice at an unknown cost, or a file name the run refuses, passed there but was refused by `check-tt ACCOUNT` and by the run. A file the run reads for its account now gets all of the account's checks. (TJ-0007)
- A `.tt` file the run refuses by its name was listed with status `ok` (and 0 errors in `--json`), and the closing line counted it as a line. Its row now shows the error, and the closing line counts problems: "N problems the run refuses". (TJ-0012)
- `tjs check-tt` split lines at form feeds and Unicode line separators inside a line. That numbered every later line differently from `tjs run` and turned a comment's tail into a false error. Lines are now numbered as the run and an editor number them. (TJ-0029)
- `tjs checklist --run` left the ".tt lines" step unchecked while a `.tt` line stopped the run. The step is now attention, naming the first line `tjs check-tt` finds. (TJ-0032)
- `tjs check-tt inputs/margin/x.tt` (the name check-tt itself prints) failed with "no such file" in the default years layout, and so did a path relative to `-C DIR`. A relative FILE is now looked for from the shell's folder, then from the project's folder and its inputs folder. (TJ-0033, TJ-0041)
- A `.tt` line with too few fields said "malformed .tt line (IndexError: list index out of range)". It now names the missing fields and the action's form, for example "BUYSELL needs PRICE and TOTAL after CUR (BUYSELL DATE TIME SYMBOL QTY CUR PRICE TOTAL [FEE] [xSIZE])". Other malformed-line messages no longer show a Python exception name or a `\n`. (TJ-0128)
- A form feed, a vertical tab or a Unicode line separator (U+2028, U+2029, U+0085) inside a `.tt` line, often pasted into a comment, made the run's readers of `RENAME`, `JOURNAL`, `ALLOWLOSS`, `INKIND`, the FX-on-cash lines and `OPENING … cost=unknown` read the text after it as a line of their own, and book it. For example, a rename written in a comment moved a position to the new symbol, so its later sale was left out of `taxjson sum`. Every `.tt` reader now ends a line at a line feed only, as the converter does. Positions, ACB, a superficial-loss or wash-sale denial, an in-kind move or the FX gain on cash can change for such a file. (TJ-0203)
- `tjs init` (and `--demo`), `tjs new-year` and getting-started step 7 said plain `tjs checklist` runs the checks; it only shows the last run's verdicts, so a first project showed every step unchecked. They now name `tjs checklist --run` (TJ-0011).
- `tjs checklist --json` is now `schema_version` 3 and `tjs years --json` `schema_version` 2. v0.35.0 renamed `skipped` to `forced` under the old numbers, and settings.md still documented the years' `marks` as `{"done", "skipped"}` (TJ-0030, TJ-0045).
- `tjs checklist --skip ID`, removed in v0.35.0, failed with a bare "unrecognized arguments". It now stops naming `tjs checklist --done ID --force`, and troubleshooting.md has the message (TJ-0042).
- The `--done` / `--undo` / `--reset` confirmations no longer start with "taxjson checklist:"; their later lines are flush-left and wrapped (TJ-0174).
- A `--section` or `--only` view with nothing left ended "Nothing left to do now: the [?] items are yours to run and read" with no [?] item in view. It now names its scope and the next open step elsewhere, and names [?] items only when there are some (TJ-0048).
- Outside any git repository, the inputs-committed step named `git status`, which fails there. It now says `git init ..` (the folder holding the year folders) or `git init`, then commit (TJ-0102).
- export-coverage counted the broker's own open positions but said `taxjson list` "lists them", and that list showed every source's. It now says "N open position(s) in <broker>'s rows" and that the list is the account's (TJ-0114).
- A project with no run yet showed about eleven differently worded blocked lines, several saying the command twice. It now shows one: "! 16 blocked (4 inputs-frozen, 5 export-coverage +14 more): no books yet — tjs run" (TJ-0178).
- A US project's tobase-map step explained itself with Canadian rules (ACB pool, superficial-loss rule) and now gives a US reason. `--done 1099-b` / `1099-div` (also 1099-da, 1099-int) name the slip steps (TJ-0185).
- inputs-frozen said "January 2025 is not in the books yet" when the books held a January trade. It now names the cutoff it checks: "not through 2025-01-31 yet" (TJ-0188).

### Fixed: year end: close-year, new-year, migrate, years and check-filed

- A year frozen by `close-year` no longer calls the later years' rows of its copied exports impossible. `tjs check-dates`, its checklist step and the re-close gate said "far outside the project year" and to "fix the source file" (exit 1). They now count those rows, as they did before the freeze. (TJ-0013)
- `tjs close-year --force` no longer locks books whose last run did not finish. Before, it wrote an empty `filed/<year>/reports/` that `tjs compare filed` never matched. Those books are refused, and the refusal no longer offers `--force`. (TJ-0015)
- With an account deferred at a pending election, close-year offered `--force`. `--force` then failed on "STALE" wash gains and blamed an `--account` rerun that never happened. The refusal now names the deferred account and `taxjson elect --pending`, and offers `--force` only where it would lock the books. (TJ-0148)
- On a terminal, close-year asked "Lock 2025 anyway?" without naming the checklist items it was asking about; they showed only with `--details`. They are now listed above the question. (TJ-0035)
- In a git repository, close-year locked a year whose inputs were not committed, though the docs list uncommitted inputs as a stop. Now it asks on a terminal, and piped it refuses unless `--yes` is given. (TJ-0090)
- The close-year gate printed "- handoff: — `taxjson handoff`" with no reason. It now says "1 carry-forward input(s) differ from the 2024 record". (TJ-0117)
- In the years layout, with a crypto send decided, every run, `check-filed` and `compare filed` of a closed year reported `inputs/crypto/crypto_sends.tt` as a changed frozen input to "restore". close-year now freezes the generated file with the year. A year closed before is compared without it, so no re-close is needed. (TJ-0089)
- The replaced-lock warning of `close-year --force` printed the disposition count with cents ("13.00 -> 14.00"). It now prints a whole count. (TJ-0189)
- close-year's CLOSED block and `tjs years` showed realized and disallowed a cent or two off `tjs sum`'s RETURN row, which is what you file. They now show the RETURN row's figures, which close-year records in the lock. `check-filed` still compares the engine totals, and no filed figure changes. (TJ-0192)
- A corrected export saved in the shared folder that changes only a filed year's sale showed nowhere: the filed year read its copy, and the next year's handoff said everything carried over. The filed year's `check-filed`, and its run, now name each shared export that changed or lost a row of that year since the close. The filing docs say where such a correction shows. (TJ-0091)
- Run in the folder holding the year folders, `tjs check-filed` sent you to the newest year, usually still open, which answered that no lock existed. Both answers now name the year folders that hold a lock (`tjs -C 2024 check-filed`). (TJ-0092)
- `tjs new-year 2026` with no 2025 folder copied from 2024 and left a gap
  in the years. It now stops with `Error: 2025 has no year folder: start it
  first` and names `taxjson new-year 2025`. (TJ-0036)
- `tjs migrate --to-years` added exports_dir (and inputs_dir, tobase_map, a
  raised requires_taxjson) unaligned at the end of `[settings]`, so `tjs format
  --check` failed right after it. A file in the template layout now stays in
  it. (TJ-0049)
- `tjs migrate --to-years` and `tjs new-year` printed lines past the width
  (up to 204 columns piped). They now wrap at the width, with later lines
  flush-left. (TJ-0190)
- `tjs migrate`'s tobase.map merge showed its plan, naming a file it was
  about to refuse (not UTF-8) as "the one kept". The refusal now comes first,
  and every refused copy names its byte and offset. (TJ-0050)
- The tobase.map merge told a filed year that reads its own frozen copy to
  "add the setting there", which would point a filed year at the shared file.
  It now says the year reads its own frozen copy and leaves it alone. The dry
  run says "would set". (TJ-0086)
- A filed year closed with its inputs frozen whose taxjson.toml names the
  shared `inputs_dir` or `tobase_map` again was only an Info note, though the
  books read the shared files. It is now a `Warning:` naming the line to
  delete, `tjs run --strict` stops on it, and `tjs years` shows the year's own
  frozen tobase.map with the problem. (TJ-0108)
- An earlier year's lock kept in a later year's `filed/` was told that the
  later year's own settings "name the shared folders again". It now gets one
  note saying the lock is checked from the inputs the later project reads.
  (TJ-0087)
- The getting-started steps for folding years into a shared folder told a
  frozen year to add `inputs_dir`, which unfreezes it. They now say to copy
  the inputs and tobase.map into the year's folder and leave `inputs_dir`
  unset. (TJ-0088)
- `tjs new-year` listed every key of the commented-out `[estimate]` /
  `[instalments]` tables twice (the template's example and last year's value).
  Last year's value now takes the example's place, so each key is listed once.
  (TJ-0191)
- `tjs years` showed a filed year as clean while its `tjs run` warned `filed 2024 DRIFTED`. The drift check (`tjs run`, `tjs check-filed`) now keeps its verdict in `work/filed_check.state`, and `years` shows `filed … DRIFTED` with "! 2024: its last run DRIFTED from filed/2024.json — tjs -C 2024 check-filed"; `years --json` has `drifted` (TJ-0159).
- `tjs years` offered a filed year's differences from the newest year as a step (`What differs: tjs years --diff`), and `tjs align --write` in the filed year silently changed the settings its lock was closed with, which left a permanent "frozen input(s) changed" note. Those differences are now marked `(filed)` with no step, and `align --write` in a filed year warns before it writes (TJ-0103).
- With a filed year's lock unreadable, `tjs years` told you to `tjs migrate` its frozen `tobase.map`, and `migrate` pointed the year back at the shared file. The year now stays frozen while its taxjson.toml carries close-year's freeze note (TJ-0158).
- A damaged lock's line in `tjs years` was cut mid-word at 80 characters ("not a finite numb"). It is now cut at a clause or word within 100 columns (TJ-0051).
- `tjs years` in a single-folder project headed its output with the parent folder's path. It names the project's folder (TJ-0116).
- docs/settings.md's `years --json` schema now lists `tobase_frozen` and `drifted`, and `marks` as `done` / `forced` (TJ-0193).
- After `close-year`, inputs-frozen stayed the next step and said to download exports into `inputs/<account>/`, the frozen copy. Once the year is filed the step is done; it names the gap the year was filed with and that a late export means an amendment (TJ-0143).
- lock-committed said "committed" while an older `.gitignore`'s unanchored `reports/` hid `filed/<year>/reports/` from git. It now needs attention and names the ignored path, the rule and the fix (TJ-0147). Outside any git repository it names `git init` (`git -C .. init` from a year folder) instead of `git status filed/`, which fails there (TJ-0205).
- next-year in a single-folder project named `tjs new-year 2025` (which refuses there), an `init --single` folder, an `align` that failed, and a `prior_year_record` path that assumed the folder's name. It now names `tjs migrate --to-years`, then `tjs new-year` (TJ-0142). Once the next year exists, its detail names `tjs checklist --run` (TJ-0204).

### Fixed: carryover, handoff, the estimate and minimum tax

- `tjs handoff` no longer says "it is in neither return. Add it here." for an early-January row the broker corrected after the closed year's project read it. A row with the same account, action, symbol, date and quantity is that row, and a note gives both amounts. Following the old advice booked the purchase twice. (TJ-0014)
- `tjs handoff`'s cost choice now gives the corrected cost for "amend … and open with". It used to give the closed record's cost for both choices. (TJ-0144)
- `tjs handoff --prior` with an older record now names this project's year in its header, not the record's year + 1. (TJ-0115)
- `tjs handoff` no longer reports a T1A carry-back of this year's loss, recorded as `[carryover] claimed` under the closed year, as a mismatch with that year's record. That mismatch made handoff exit 1 and blocked `tjs close-year`. The part this project's loss carries back is taken out before the claim is compared. (TJ-0078)
- `tjs estimate` in a loss year now carries forward only what `[carryover] claimed` does not carry back: "Unused capital losses: … (carry forward; … carried back: [carryover] claimed, T1A)". This matches carryover and the lock. (TJ-0084)
- `tjs carryover`: a closed year with no `claimed` entry now shows APPLIED as what its lock applied. It used to show 0.00 while the balance fell, and it offered that gain again ("apply up to …"). (TJ-0052)
- `tjs carryover --details` now tells you to record claims in taxjson.toml (`[carryover]` then `claimed = { … }`). It used to point to `--claimed FILE`, which `tjs carryover` rejects. (TJ-0145)
- `tjs estimate`'s INSTALMENTS block now labels the instalment shortfall "=> instalments behind … [due with the balance April 30]". It used to label it "=> balance due April 30". (TJ-0146)
- `tjs amt` / `tjs estimate`: "Recovered: ON share" is now the provincial factor times the federal amount, the share taken off basic Ontario tax. The surtax it saves is shown on a separate row; the estimate shows "[federal 900.50 + ON 221.79 + ON surtax 124.21]". The old figure was the whole Ontario tax drop, under a label that said "before ON surtax". No tax figure changes. (TJ-0016)
- `tjs option-boundary` (and the checklist step) no longer asks for a T1-ADJ once the grant year's lock, re-closed after the amendment, no longer reports the premium. (TJ-0085)
- `tjs check-filed` now exits 1 on a lock whose `fx_cash_v2` close the next year's FX-on-cash ledger refuses. It used to say OK. The ledger's repair now names the record `[settings] prior_year_record` gives. (TJ-0068)
- `tjs option-boundary`, `tjs compare filed`, the edge-cases option check and the `option_grant_timing_since` hint now apply the standard lock check. They used to read a damaged lock, or one closed under the other country, as a good one. `tjs years` now shows such a lock as "other country". (TJ-0069)

### Fixed: missing history, transfers and sanity

- `tjs find-missing-history --write-purchases` drafted a transfer-in whose row states
  a book value of 0 at a cost of 0.00. Filled in with only its date, the line booked a
  $0 lot and the sale's whole proceeds were filed as gain. The line now leaves the cost
  as `COST`, which the run refuses until you fill it in, and says the 0 is the broker's
  placeholder. If you kept such a line, check its cost (TJ-0008).
- A transfer-in the run reports only PARTLY covered by `.tt` purchases is now drafted:
  a line for the other units, at `COST`, with a note on how to price them. It used to
  be "not drafted: a line would count it twice" (TJ-0009).
- Drafts from IB's Basis no longer add a line for each sale that went short when the
  files bought shares between two of them. That gave more lines than were missing, and
  filled in they held shares the broker does not (TJ-0018).
- The drafts no longer read an arrival 11 to 45 days after an in-kind move to a
  registered account as "a move from your account": it is drafted as a purchase, as the
  run treats it (TJ-0074).
- `--write-missing-history` and `--write-purchases` refuse to write from books older
  than the inputs ("the books in work/ are older than the inputs ... nothing was
  written"). Run right after a `.tt` purchase was added, they used to write an
  unknown-cost opening for the sale it covers. `tjs find-missing-history`,
  `tjs sanity` and `tjs transfers` now warn when the books are not the clean result of
  the current inputs (TJ-0077).
- A written option booked at grant (`option_grant_timing_since`) with no purchase in
  your files is no longer called "NOT in the totals" while its premium is in them. It
  is a short covered (a Warning) and listed under `no_purchase_in_totals`; the figures
  are unchanged (TJ-0017).
- The run's closing list counts one $0-cost lot that is part sold and part held once:
  "1 position at a $0 cost (QZK.TO)", not "2 positions ... (QZK.TO, QZK.TO)"
  (TJ-0044).
- The `--write-missing-history` note is wrapped at the output width (TJ-0175).
- `tjs transfers`' TYPE column shows the kind of transfer: IB's `ACATS` /
  `InterDepot` / `Internal`, a crypto exchange's `withdrawal`, else `transfer-in` /
  `transfer-out`. It used to show a slug of the broker's description, with the other
  account's number in it on Questrade rows. `--json` is unchanged (TJ-0055).
- Its `! ` lines fit in 100 columns ("N transfer-in(s) with no cost (…)", "N
  transfer-in(s) only partly covered, NOT booked (…)"), with the fix in `--details`
  (TJ-0043).
- `tjs sanity` refuses books (`work/<account>_base.json`) that are `{}`,
  a bare list or lack a transactions list. It used to read them as an
  empty history and could certify a wrong dated snapshot as OK
  (TJ-0010).
- `tjs sanity` no longer says "INCOMPLETE: 1 account(s) … not checked: fix
  the paths" for a holdings/ snapshot of an account that was compared
  with its own `holdings = [...]` files. That note is an Info, in `tjs
  run` too, and `--json` `complete` stays true. INCOMPLETE now counts the
  unchecked accounts and the uncompared snapshots separately (TJ-0020).
- `tjs run` no longer says "positions match the broker's holdings files
  (every checked account)" when an account's configured holdings file is
  missing. That account is named as unchecked, and `sanity --json` lists
  it in `accounts_not_checked` (TJ-0064).
- `tjs sanity` with no holdings file: `--json` prints JSON (it printed
  text). UNCHECKED counts every account with positions, registered ones
  too. `--details` lists them. The hint mentions holdings/README.txt only
  where that file exists (TJ-0135).
- The refusal of one broker account's snapshots at several dates gave
  advice that only repeated the error. It now says to keep one snapshot
  per broker account, or names a working command for one date (TJ-0065).
- `tjs sanity` says when it sums different broker accounts' snapshots
  from different dates while the books changed after the earliest one,
  so a quantity difference there reads as that change. The compare
  itself is unchanged (TJ-0066).
- When sanity finds a difference, `tjs checklist` names the differing
  positions ("2 differ: ZZB.TO (margin), …"). It used to show the last
  line of the cost section (TJ-0082, TJ-0094).
- In a project with positions and no holdings file, `tjs checklist`'s
  sanity step needs attention. It was a confirm step that `--done sanity`
  could close with nothing compared (TJ-0136, TJ-0195).
- The "cost is not compared" note for a holding whose cost field is not a
  number keeps its reason in the default one-line view (TJ-0160).

### Fixed: FX-on-cash ledger v2 and corporate actions

- **Kraken reward wallets.** A Kraken reward paid to a wallet asset (`USDC.F`,
  `USD.HOLD`) no longer replaces the spot balance in ledger v2's statement
  balance. That false gap made the year NOT COMPUTED. Each asset code keeps
  its own balance, summed into the currency. (backlog TJ-0019)
- **Coinbase rewards priced in CAD.** A USDC reward that Coinbase prices in
  CAD now brings its US dollars into the US-dollar pool, at the income's CAD
  value. The year was refused with a gap it called a missing deposit. If you
  declared the reward with a `CASHMOVE` line, remove it. (backlog TJ-0038)
- **Moves between your own accounts.** An own move that the receiving broker
  books up to 7 days before the sending one is no longer refused ("only 0.00
  USD had left one of them before it"). A chain of own moves on one day (a to
  b to c) no longer makes up a debt and a gain on the middle account. A move
  still refused now says why. (backlog TJ-0067)
- **Prior-year record of the other country.** A US year after a Canadian
  record opens from its `CASHOPEN` lines, as the refusal advised. Before, the
  lines did not clear it, and a record closed under the default ledger (no
  pool to carry) was refused too. (backlog TJ-0022)
- **Books that end the year at zero.** `close-year` with ledger v2 now records
  these books. Every later year used to ask for a `CASHOPEN … 0 0` line for
  them and to re-close a year already closed with this ledger. (backlog
  TJ-0028)
- **`tjs fx-cash --cash-events` listing.** A deposit declared by a `.tt`
  `CASHMOVE` is listed once, with the line under DECLARED BY. When nothing was
  read, the list says "None read from the exports or .tt lines." (backlog
  TJ-0054, TJ-0168)
- **`$0 cost` warning after a hand-booked fraction.** The `.tt` BUY of an
  s.86.1 spin-off's fraction at 0 and its SELL for the cash, the documented
  fix for an RBC cash in lieu, no longer brings a "position at a $0 cost"
  warning or a find-missing-history "inflated gain" row. The pooled cost the
  election set covers the fraction. (backlog TJ-0101)
- **`tjs sanity` before the cash in lieu is paid.** Between an s.86.1
  spin-off and its cash in lieu (a December spin-off paid in January),
  `tjs sanity` no longer reports the fraction as a QTY_MISMATCH with exit 1.
  A `fraction` line names it. (backlog TJ-0149)
- **`tjs spinoffs` labels.** The broker's US-dollar value per share is now
  labelled USD; it was labelled CAD. The ratio counts a fraction paid in cash
  ("0.1 new per share (10.5 for 105)"), and a "cash in lieu" line gives the
  fraction and the cash. `tjs elect --pending` gives the same line. (backlog
  TJ-0134, TJ-0166)

### Fixed: broker files and parsers

- Two overlapping downloads pasted into one export file (the header repeated; for Webull, the statement's Account Number preamble) had the rows both downloads hold booked twice: silently for Webull and the generic importer, and for Questrade with a false "the export holds rows of 2 Questrade accounts" warning. Such a file is now refused ("line N: the header repeats here — two downloads pasted into one file …"); save each download as its own file and the overlap is read once. Pasted parts that share no row are read as before. RBC now says that the header repeats instead of "Amount 'Amount' is not a number", and a single repeated Questrade header line is no longer counted as a second account. (TJ-0099)
- Two Coinbase or Kraken downloads of one account that disagree on one row (a restated price, amount, quantity or date under the same ID / txid) kept the version of the file whose name sorts first, with no message. The run now stops and names both files, the masked id and both versions, as it already did for one file. (TJ-0071)
- Kraken: a line holding only spaces (often the last line) is skipped like an empty line; it was refused as "a truncated or misaligned row (a missing fee would read as 0)". (TJ-0040)
- Kraken: the UNBOOKED warning for a trades row whose type is neither buy nor sell no longer says "the file is refused until it is gone": the rest of the file is booked, and only `--strict` stops. (TJ-0026)
- Kraken: a ledgers export's refusal (for example a missing `fee` column) is now headed by the ledger's name, not by the trades file being parsed beside it, and the trades file's own row errors no longer print its name twice. (TJ-0164)
- IB: a section refused for a missing `Code` column gives a reason that fits ("a cancelled row (code Ca) reads as a new event"), not "a missing money column read as 0". Every other non-money column gets a fitting reason too. (TJ-0053)
- The generic importer's date error now names the line and the mapping ("ws.csv line 2: unparseable date '2024-02-01': it does not match [formats].date = '%d/%m/%Y' (ws.csv.toml)"), and `tjs sanity`'s unreadable-books error now starts with the damaged work/ file instead of "taxjson.toml:". (TJ-0057)
- A row the schema check refuses (for example a Questrade Buy with an empty Symbol) is now named by file and line ("questrade_demo.csv line 3: BUYSELL (no symbol) 2024-03-20: missing required field 'symbol'") and the message says what to do. It used to give a masked row id, which cannot be searched for, and a double space. This covers Questrade and the generic importer. (TJ-0124)
- The FX rates window now reads 8-digit dates under a header written in capitals with its words run together (`TRADEDATE`, `SETTLEDATE`). Such a header was missed, so in a file that also held a date of another shape the window started too late and the run stopped with "no exchange rate". (TJ-0072)
- `examples/ib_demo.csv` is now the demo project's file, with its Cash Report, so a project built from `examples/` no longer warns "no Cash Report, so its cash is not reconciled". (TJ-0180)

### Fixed: planning views, prices and the radar

- US `[[distributions]]`: `tjs run` no longer warns "ATTENTION … it misses the lots of the trade(s) in between (bought N on …)" for a purchase that straddles the record date (traded on or before it, settled after it). Such a purchase is not the holder of record's and rightly takes none, and the placement was already exact. The warning still names a trade that settles by the record date. (TJ-0021, TJ-0027)
- `tjs harvest`: a position whose quote currency the books have no rate for is named in one warning, symbol first, with the fix that works: add the currency to `source_currencies` in taxjson.toml, then `tjs run`. The run never fetched a currency only a `QUOTE` line uses, so "run `taxjson run`" fixed nothing. Before, the warning came once per account and the default view cut off the symbol. `tjs harvest --json` now lists every position it left out, and why, under `omitted`. (TJ-0024)
