  line), as the query with the suffix does. The bare ticker answered SAFE.
- **sell-check gives the SIMILAR caveat for a look-alike bought in the
  past 30 days only in a registered account or IRA** (Canada and the
  US). The radar files such a holding CLEAR, so sell-check said SAFE
  while the run warned about the pair; the radar's JSON row now has
  `sheltered_buy`.
- **An s.86.1 spin-off's cash in lieu sold by hand in a `.tt` file ends
  the UNBOOKED warning.** The warning named that fix but never read the
  `.tt` files, so it printed on every run and `run --strict` stopped on
  it. It now names the last day such a sale is read.
- **`scripts/release.sh --prepare` names the upgrade notes**: it renames
  `docs/upgrading.md`'s `### Unreleased` to the tag, as it does the
  CHANGELOG's. v0.31.0 shipped its own note under "Unreleased".

## v0.31.1 (2026-10-22)

### Changed: tax figures

- **An s.86.1 spin-off paid cash for a fraction sells the fraction at the
  cash, on its share of the allocated cost** (Questrade and RBC,
  `CA-CORP-05`). The spun-off shares and the fraction take the full
  allocated cost and the parent gives up all of it; the fraction's gain is
  the cash less its share. RBC's cash-in-lieu row was not booked, and
  Questrade's own $0 purchase and sale of the fraction is replaced, so it
  is sold once. A taxable spin-off, IB and the US §355 path are unchanged.
- **US futures: a partial close is taken FIFO in trade-date order**
  (`US-FUT-01`), not settlement-date order, matching the US engine. Only
  a generic CSV whose settle dates ran out of trade order was affected:
  the close now takes the contract traded first, so its gain moves, up
  or down, by the difference between that contract's price and the one
  it took before (audit 102).

### Fixed: release tooling

- **The release cut and `promote.sh` wait for a CI run still going** instead of
  calling it failed: `scripts/github-ci.sh` polls the run through `gh api`
  rather than `gh run watch`, which a fine-grained token cannot use (it
  reads check-run annotations).
- **`promote.sh` twice within one second no longer fails** with "tag
  'channels-…' already exists": the second fast-lane tag waits for the
  next second's name.
- **`scripts/lock_deps.py` takes a relative `--uv` path** (it ran uv from
  a temporary folder, where the path did not resolve).

### Changed

- **Dependency locks regenerated** (the 7-day cooldown, to 2026-10-15),
  with `certifi` 2026.10.19 let past it for PYSEC-2026-4320:
  `scripts/lock_deps.py --security-update PKG` lets one named package past
  the cooldown for a security fix and names it in the locks' header.
  `pip-audit` finds no known vulnerability in any lock.

### Fixed: option statistics and option-yield

- **Option statistics: a split long option is counted once.** A plain split of an option you bought no longer doubles the contracts held, so a later over-sale and buy-back shows as a written-option trade in `tjs stats` / `tjs win-rates`.
- **Option statistics: an assigned put's premium follows a split or ticker change of the shares.** The premium taken out of the delivered shares' later sales is scaled through a split and carried across a rename, instead of being drawn at the old rate or stranded.
- **Option statistics and option-yield: a write that nets less than its commission is a loss.** A sale with a negative net amount keeps its sign in `tjs stats` and `tjs option-yield`, as the engine books it; buy-back amounts are still read as money paid.
- **Option statistics: an assigned call's premium comes out of its own share sale.** The share leg is chosen as the engine pairs it (marked, at the strike, the delivered quantity, nearest), not an unrelated sale up to 3 days earlier, so the right trade and month carry it in `tjs win-rates`.
- **Option statistics and option-yield: a series renamed into another stays first in, first out.** Contracts moved into a series that already has open contracts queue by their open date.
- **Option statistics: exercised long options are counted in the period asked for.** `tjs stats YEAR --details` and `exercised_long_options` in the JSON no longer count exercises from other years.
- **Option-yield: a split later on the day a contract was opened counts once.** A split stamped after the open on the same day re-denominates the contracts, instead of skewing the P/L and leaving negative contracts open.
- **Option-yield: a contract closed in another currency than it was opened in is money-unknown.** Its premium and P/L are blank instead of one currency subtracted from the other, and a `!` line names the row to check (audit 37).
- **Option-yield: a contract renamed into another strike's series shows the new strike.** An RBC special-dividend strike adjustment (or a ratio-1 `SPLIT` into another series) kept the old strike, and the strike-notional yield used it (audit 81).

### Fixed: dividend estimates, income dating and the hand-off

- **div-estimate: a weekly payer held at two brokers stays weekly.** Postings of one payment a few days apart were chained week to week, so four weekly payments became one payment of four times the amount; a posting more than five days after an earlier one of the same account now starts the next payment.
- **div-estimate: a positional window has the 120-month limit.** `tjs div-estimate 100000y` printed a traceback; a window over 120 months is now refused with one error line, like `--months 121`.
- **div-estimate: two broker accounts in one account are not doubled.** With `combined_broker_accounts = true`, the same dividend paid to both broker accounts on one day was read as twice the per-share amount; each broker account is now a holding of its own.
- **January ROC warning: the .tt pair must be in the same account.** The two ADJUST lines that silence a Canadian trust's January return-of-capital warning now count only in that ROC's account and currency; the same pair in another account no longer hides it.
- **handoff: Dec 31 / early-January rows are matched one to one, per account.** An identical income row in another account no longer stands in for a row the closed year never had, and one row here no longer answers two identical rows of the closed year's record; both now give the "in neither return" warning.

### Fixed: FX-on-cash ledger v2 and importers

- **Two broker accounts no longer share one cash book.** In the FX-on-cash ledger v2, two accounts of one broker in an account folder whose hashed ids begin with the same 4 characters got one merged book that no `at=` could name. Their books now get longer names (`ib:31355`, `ib:31357`); books without such a clash keep their names.
- **A CASHOPEN with no book is reported.** In the FX-on-cash ledger v2, a foreign-currency `CASHOPEN` in a `.tt` file whose folder holds several books, with no `at=` or `CASHBOOK` line, was dropped silently. It is now a problem naming the line and saying to add `at=<book>` or a `CASHBOOK` line.
- **FXCONV with `value=` needs no exchange rate.** In the FX-on-cash ledger v2, a conversion between two foreign currencies that gives its base-currency `value=` was refused when the from-currency had no rate on file for that day; the value now prices it.
- **Generic importer: a futures sale at a negative price is booked.** An export with unsigned quantities refused a futures sale at a negative price (which pays cash) as "a buy by its own signs"; it is now read like the same sale with a signed quantity.
- **ALLOWLOSS refuses a decimal-comma quantity.** `ALLOWLOSS <date> <symbol> 1,5 …` was read as 15 units; a quantity is now read like a `.tt` row's (`1,000` is a thousand, `1,5` is refused with the line named).
- **Ledger v2, Kraken: the cash reader reads the ledger as the parser does.** An upper-case header is read, a missing column stops naming the file (it gave no cash events), a day's balance is the one after its latest row by time (not file order), and a fee is booked in its `feecurrency` (audit 71, 72, 78).
- **Ledger v2: one cash event two files settle on different dates is kept once with a Warning** naming both files and both dates, instead of silently keeping one file's date (audit 86).
- **Ledger v2: a `.tt` file that cannot be read is named** ("inputs/<account>/<file>: cannot be read (…)") instead of skipped, which refused the ledger for the wrong reason (audit 91).
- **Ledger v2: a futures commission leaves the cash on its own fill's date.** An opening fee was valued at the close date's rate; the books' gains are unchanged (audit 103).
- **ALLOWLOSS: a line dated the settlement day of only some fills of a sale names none.** When a same-day sale's fills settle on different days, a line dated one fill's settlement day overrode that fill alone; the message now gives the sale's trade date (audit 88).
- **crypto-sends: a send's fair value uses the full-precision price.** The value and the `crypto_sends.tt` proceeds came from the six-digit displayed price (at most a few parts per million); lines already written are kept (audit 47).

### Fixed: opening, sanity, holdings and views

- **Export gap check follows splits.** A split between a broker export's end and the year end now scales the shares left, so selling part of the post-split shares no longer hides the missing-export warning. A ticker change is followed to the new symbol.
- **`tjs opening` writes exact quantities.** A quantity with more than 8 significant digits (e.g. 12345.678912 or 123456789) is written exactly instead of being rounded (`1.2345679e+08`).
- **Impossible dates in a holdings TOML are refused.** A `[meta] as_of`, `generated_at` or `acquired` that is not a real calendar day (2025-02-30) is now an error naming the field. `tjs sanity` used to accept it and report clean.
- **`tjs sanity` keeps a holdings file's date when its cost is malformed.** A non-numeric cost field no longer makes sanity compare the latest books instead of the file's `as_of` date. The quantities are compared at that date, and a note says the cost was not compared.
- **`tjs splits` sees shares received through a ticker change.** A split of a renamed symbol now shows the holdings before and after it, instead of "nothing held".
- **`taxjson-export` keeps a holdings TOML's contract size.** Reading a holdings TOML back (`--report`, `--holdings-toml`) keeps its `contract_multiplier` instead of falling back to 100 (or unknown, for a futures option).
- **Huge look-back periods mean "all".** A period like `24311m` or `2026y` on a period-aware command (`tjs events ...`) now covers the whole history instead of crashing with a traceback.
- **RBC Holdings Export: a per-share cost column is read per share.** 'Book Cost Per Share', 'Average Book Cost' and 'Book Cost/Share' were read as the position's total; a cost label that is neither a total nor per share is refused, naming it (audit 46).
- **Sanity: the income-on-unheld-shares check follows renames by date,** so a reused old ticker no longer carries shares that left with an earlier rename (audit 61).
- **`tjs compare`: a moved account figure is a difference even when every report file matches.** The table is shown, `--json` `different` is true and the exit is 1 (audit 66).
- **`tjs compare`: an unreadable report file or folder is an error naming it,** never counted as removed or left out of the snapshot (audit 84).
- **Prices: a non-finite quote from any tier is ignored** and the next tier asked; nothing non-finite is cached (audit 57).
- **Prices: an IBKR hit is cached under the spelling IB priced,** not a ticker.map `QUOTE` remap, so an offline run no longer serves it as the remapped symbol's price (audit 69).

### Fixed: slips, carryover and tools

- **Loss carryover: one year typed two ways is an error.** `[carryover] claimed = { 2023 = 100, 02023 = 200 }` silently kept one of the two amounts; every command now stops with "2023 is given twice" and asks for one line.
- **`tjs fetch`: a malformed Questrade response is a one-line error.** A token or API reply that was valid JSON but not an object (an array or a string, e.g. from a broken proxy) crashed with a traceback.
- **`taxjson-diff --by` a list or dict field works.** Matching on a structured field such as `wash_replacements` crashed with "unhashable type"; it now matches on the field's canonical JSON.
- **`tjs slip-audit`: a foreign T5008 with no exchange rate no longer shows 0.00.** Its slip proceeds and cost now show "—" with a note that the FX cache has no rate for the year (`tjs run` fetches it), instead of an unmarked 0.00 total.
- **`tjs slip-audit`: weekly dividends whose dates drift all match.** When IB's dividends report and the export dated one security's weekly payments 4 or more days apart, one payment showed as missing from the books and another as missing from the slip; payments now pair in date order.
- **`tjs slip-audit --import-cra`: a T5 two broker accounts match equally is not guessed.** It was placed in whichever account came first; it is now left unplaced as "ambiguous", naming `broker_account` in slips.toml as the fix (CA-SLIP-04).
- **IB dividends report: withholding and base-currency amounts are checked against the Summary row,** like Gross; a mismatch is listed with the report's problems (audit 54).
- **IB dividends report: a blank GrossInBase beside a Gross is refused,** naming the line, instead of counting the payment as 0 in a CAD-base account's boxes (audit 55).
- **IB dividends report: an impossible date is refused,** naming the file, line and value; a USD-base report showed a traceback (audit 56).
- **IB dividends report: amounts are read strictly:** '1,5' is refused, not read as 15 (audit 90).
- **`slip-audit --import-cra`: a known box whose figure is not an amount refuses the slip** instead of importing it without that box; a wrapped label word is still skipped (audit 111).
- **slip-audit: payments are matched within one currency.** A payment whose only nearby book row is in another currency is a currency mismatch (`payments.currency_differs`), not a match (audit 94).
- **slip-audit: a security's slips in two currencies are compared and suggested per currency,** never summed in the last slip's currency (audit 95).
- **slip-audit: a `.tt` ROC line with no `record=` is redated by its own listing's distribution,** another listing of the root only when its own paid nothing (audit 93).
- **slip-audit: the "books already hold" note names the row's pay and record dates,** so a prior year's row shows as one (audit 97).
- **slip-audit: the annual-average rate ignores a non-finite cached rate** (audit 100).

## v0.31.0 (2026-10-21)

### Added

- **`sum --json` and `form-export --json` say whether the figures are
  complete.** A `readiness` record carries `complete` and the open
  `issues` (books not built from the current inputs, sales left out of
  or in no total, a cost or quantity the engine's conservation check
  found the books lost track of), each with the command that resolves
  it; `sum` prints a conservation problem as a `! ` line, which reached
  only the account's `.sum` diagnostics before. The US engine's
  sub-1e-8-unit rows that carry money count as one.
- **`taxjson compare`: what changed since an earlier run.** Every
  full `taxjson run` keeps the reports it replaces (`work/compare/
  prev/`, with the inputs fingerprint they were built from);
  `compare` diffs the current `reports/` against them, a snapshot
  saved with `--save NAME`, or the reports as filed (`filed`): the
  account figures that moved, the report files that differ and the
  inputs that changed; exit 1 on a difference. `--details` adds the
  unified diffs.
- **`close-year` freezes the inputs.** With exports shared by every
  year, the files the filed books were built from are copied into the
  year's own `inputs/` (and the shared `tobase.map` beside
  `ticker.map`), and the year reads that copy from then on
  (`inputs_dir` / `tobase_map` commented out), so the filed year can
  be rebuilt as filed while the shared exports move on. The lock
  records every input's hash, `check-filed` names a frozen input that
  changed since, `reports/` is kept as `filed/<year>/reports/`,
  `new-year` points the next year at the shared folders again and
  `migrate --to-years` gives a frozen year its own copy.
- **ticker.map `SIMILAR A B [C ...]`: look-alike funds watched
  together.** Two issuers' funds on one index, or a fund and its
  Canadian wrapper, stay separate securities (their own pools, nothing
  denied: the superficial-loss rule reaches identical property, §1091
  substantially identical securities, and whether such a pair is one is
  your call), but with the line a loss on one with another bought in
  the window is a Warning of every `taxjson run`, a manual item of the
  checklist's wash-reviewed step, a caveat in `buy-check` and
  `sell-check` (SAFE\*), the flagged listings in `rebuy --details`
  and a `SIMILAR` block in `wash-radar` (tax-logic CA-SL-20 /
  US-WASH-26; docs/settings.md).

### Changed

- **`stats 2y`, `winners all`, `ccd-sum 2023`: a window outside the
  tax year reads the full history.** `stats`, `win-rates`, `winners`,
  `losers`, `ccd-sum`, `leaps` and `leaps-sum` read the tax year's
  gains files, which hold one year; a wider window warned that the
  rows outside it were missing and showed the year alone. Such a
  window now builds `work/<account>_gains_all.json` on demand from
  the same consolidated base-currency book the tax year's gains come
  from (ticker.map's TOBASE pooling, per-transaction FX, the same
  engine flags; rebuilt when the book, the config or the engine is
  newer) and reads that, said in an `Info:` line: the rows inside the
  tax year equal the filing file's, the superficial-loss / wash-sale
  denials are the engine's own within each account (the
  cross-account pass runs for the tax year), and the basis reads
  `pre-wash, full history`. The default window and `--json` are
  unchanged.
- **Output audit (2026-10): crisper default views.** Every command's
  text output was reviewed against docs/output-style.md. Legends are
  one or two lines directly above their table (`ccd-sum`, `winners` /
  `losers`, `leaps`, `leaps-sum`, `fees`, `gains`, `shares`); the lines
  after a table are aligned `label:  value` figures (`divs-sum`,
  `trades-sum`, `wash-sales`, `winners`, `list`, `fx-cash`, `estimate`)
  or one-line `! ` items; `sanity` says which accounts were not compared
  in one line and shows both quantities at one precision; `audit`
  prints the ACB pool history as one compact table and separates its
  account groups with a blank line; `fees-sum` sub-tables are
  flush-left with `-` for a rate with no units; titles that named every
  account (`stats`, `win-rates`, the run's pooling step) count them
  instead; the `--details` explanations of `rebuy`, `wash-radar`,
  `harvest`, `div-estimate`, `find-missing-history`, `t1135` and
  `carryover` are one-line bullets; empty states say `None in the
  books.`; the Kraken, harvest and instalments errors are one `Error:`
  line with a one-line hint. `--json` is unchanged.

### Fixed: engine, opening balances and holdings

- **A share position under a millionth of a share is still a holding
  when it carries cost.** The Canadian engine read it as flat, so its
  sale opened a short and the cost was stranded out of every total;
  it is closed at its cost (2026-10 audit 101; docs/limits.md).
- **The `tjs fetch` holdings snapshot carries each holding's
  currency**, so `taxjson opening` can use it and `sanity` compares
  like with like (audit 43); **`taxjson-export` reads back a
  mixed-currency holding** it wrote instead of a zero cost (audit 64).
- **IB partial cancellations keep the commission IB did not refund,
  and pair with the order at their own time** rather than an
  exact-size fill at another time (audit 29, 62).
- **A `[[distributions]]` entry dated on an opening snapshot's own day
  is said in a NOTE**: it is applied on top of the snapshot's cost,
  which a year-end statement often does not include yet; remove the
  entry if it does (audit 26, CA-OPEN-03).
- **An opening snapshot no longer deletes purchases of a reused
  ticker.** The cut-off follows only renames dated on or after a row's
  own date, so shares bought under an old ticker after its rename keep
  their cost and their sale is in the totals (CA-OPEN-03; 2026-10
  audit 27).
- **An option's `average_entry_price` in a holdings TOML is per
  share.** `taxjson opening` multiplies it by `multiplier`, else 100
  for an equity option, so the Questrade snapshot no longer opens a
  contract at a hundredth of its cost; `cost_per_share` stays per
  holding unit and `total_cost` is unchanged (audit 28).
- **`taxjson opening` sees OPENING lines in `.TT` files** and no
  longer opens a symbol twice (audit 30), **and refuses two broker accounts
  whose ids mask alike** (`U1***`): accounts are told apart by the
  whole id, while output shows only the masked one (audit 48).
- **`stats`, `win-rates` and `option-yield` see a missing-history
  option opening.** A long contract held before the data (a `.tt`
  `OPENING … cost=unknown` line) and sold read as a write bought back
  with a profit: the views now add the opening the gains stage adds
  (2026-10 audit 59).
- **The exchange rates cover a UTF-16 export's older rows.** The rates
  window read no date from a UTF-16 file and started at the project's
  year, so an older row stopped the run with "no exchange rate" (audit 40).

### Fixed: corporate actions

- **Two overlapping IB statements with a corrected corporate-action
  value no longer dispose of the shares twice.** A row repeated with
  another value counted as a second row of the event (twice the
  quantity, the old shares short); it is one row, the larger value is
  kept and an ATTENTION line says so. The corporate-action stage's
  ATTENTION lines (statements that disagree) now reach the run's
  console instead of only `work/*.diag`, and `run --strict` stops on
  them.
- **Two statements of one corporate event that agree on quantities
  but not on values are no longer kept by file order.** A corrected
  FMV, target value or cash in lieu in one of two overlapping
  statements of a broker account kept whichever file was read first,
  silently; the larger copy is kept whatever the order and a warning
  says what differs (2026-10 audit 104).
- **A merger held in both listings of one security in one broker
  account disposes of both.** Two equal-quantity copies on different
  listings or currencies were taken for an overlapping statement and
  one was dropped; they are two holdings under one election (audit 105).
- **A merger held at IB and at a whole-share broker in one taxjson
  account keeps IB's fractional shares whatever the file order.** The
  combined event inherited the first copy's fractional-delivery flag
  and snapped 4.5 delivered shares to 4 plus phantom cash in lieu
  (audit 106).

### Fixed: slips and CRA import

- **`--import-cra` compares the issuer before calling a slip "already
  in slips.toml"**, so another issuer's slip with equal boxes is
  added (audit 108), and an amended slip with an original's figures
  replaces it, so the older original cannot come back beside it
  (audit 110).
- **Two IB dividends reports that differ only in base-currency
  amounts are refused, not read as one** (audit 89).
- **`tjs slip-audit` tops up a partly booked return of capital with
  the rest only.** For IB's dividends report it suggested the
  payment's whole ROC again, lowering the ACB twice; it now suggests
  the difference and names the existing line to change (audit 96).
- **An issuer's second amended slip replaces the first on
  `--import-cra`.** It was added beside the earlier amendment and both
  were counted (audit 109).

### Fixed: FX on cash and crypto

- **A blank Coinbase Total is no longer a zero-cost stablecoin buy.**
  The FX-on-cash ledger v2 and the crypto-sends pool read a CAD-priced
  USDC Buy with a blank Total as costing 0; they derive it as the
  parser does and refuse a row with nothing to derive it from (2026-10
  audit 74). A USDC bought or sold for US dollars spends its fee from
  the pool (audit 73).
- **Questrade's newest-first export: same-day conversions in order.**
  Ledger v2 replayed two conversions of one day backward and paired
  legs of different conversions; rows are read in real order and the
  two adjacent legs of each conversion pair (audit 75).
- **crypto-sends reads overlapping exports once.** The stablecoin pool
  counted an entry once per overlapping Kraken ledger or Coinbase
  export holding it, diluting the average cost of a send (audit 79).
- **FX cash ledger v2: a `CASHMOVE` declaration stays in its
  `CASHBOOK`'s book, and internal transfers pair inside one
  statement.** A declaration without `at=` matched another broker
  account's identical move (audit 85); two accounts' IB statements with the
  same file name had their transfer legs paired and dropped (audit 60).

### Fixed: workflow and commands

- **The polish pass of the 2026-10 workflow audit.** An unknown flag
  after a command gets that command's usage line, not `taxjson`'s;
  `amt` relays the estimate's refusal under one `Error:` label;
  `close-year` writes one frozen note over adjacent keys, announces
  its recording as a `==>` step and puts its notes under the CARRIED
  INTO block, flush-left; `check-filed`'s title reaches a pipe before
  its warnings and its notes are flush-left; `migrate` says "nothing
  to migrate" as an `Info:` line; `migrate --to-years` says the files
  are moved (`git add -A` records the renames); `init --demo` sets a
  province, so `estimate`, `plot-tax` and the checklist's amt step run
  as they are; `init` makes the folder it scaffolds into owner-only;
  `init --help` says what `--force` overwrites and that a `.bak` is
  kept; `new-year` writes the copied `taxjson.toml` in the template
  layout; `sanity` and `opening` look for a relative FILE in the
  project folder when the shell's folder has none (`-C DIR`);
  `reconcile-slips inputs/slips/*.csv` with no slip saved says so with
  a fix; `run` with every `inputs/` folder empty names the fix on its
  one line, and `run --account` ends its line with the fix; `checklist
  --done` says a check's finding outranks the mark (`--skip` accepts
  it); the checklist's option-boundary line names the flagged
  contract's reason; `option-yield`'s past-expiry line asks for the
  export covering the expiry (not `option-boundary`, which shows it
  open), and no empty stderr line precedes its report; `slip-audit`
  names a corporate action's income "(corporate action: no export
  row)"; `handoff` prints a normalized record path; `watch`'s title
  has one parenthesis; `wash-radar`'s advice shows money with two
  decimals, and `--all` is described as it works (the OTHER rows);
  the stale-wash warning is given once per process; `redact`'s Done
  line; a shared `inputs/` that is a symlink keys its fingerprints
  as the setting names it, so a freeze no longer reads as changed
  inputs; `events` documents its dates; `commands.md` usage lines
  list `--details` / `--json` where `--help` has them, and follow
  `taxjson help`'s order; `checklist --walk` is documented as needing
  a terminal.
- **A filed year's frozen `tobase.map` was taken for a copy to merge.**
  After `close-year` froze a year, `taxjson years` asked for
  `taxjson migrate`, which (once a later year existed) removed the
  frozen copy and pointed the filed year at the shared file again. The
  frozen copy is now recognised (`years` says "frozen copy of its own
  in 2024 (filed)"; `migrate` and `update-tobase-map` leave it alone),
  and the freeze writes its note once (the second commented key gets a
  short one) (2026-10 workflow audit).
- **The scaffold `.gitignore` hid `filed/<year>/reports/`.** Its
  unanchored `reports/` line also ignored the reports as filed that
  `close-year` keeps, so they were never committed. `taxjson init` now
  writes anchored rules (`/reports/`, `/*/reports/` ...); in an
  existing project `close-year` names the line to change.
- **ticker.map `SIMILAR`: a member a `TOBASE` line moves.** The
  checklist's wash-reviewed step and `wash-radar`'s SIMILAR block read
  the group as written and missed the member booked under its other
  listing; both now read the booked symbols, as the run does.
- **Interest paid is no longer netted against interest earned.** Each
  account's `.sum` shows `CASH INTEREST` (earned) and, when there is
  any, `INTEREST PAID (not in total)` per currency: the margin interest
  for line 22100 (US: investment interest), kept out of the income
  total (`taxjson-sum-income --json`: `interest_paid_totals`). Was in
  KNOWN_ISSUES.
- **A negative futures price in a generic CSV** kept its magnitude, so
  the P/L sign was wrong; the notional's sign is now kept, as the IB
  parser keeps it. (A `.tt` line's case stays in KNOWN_ISSUES.)
- **`tips --online` probed the wrong symbols:** the 80-symbol cap was
  spent on tobase.map's alphabetical head, never the holdings. It now
  probes the held listings and their map partners, and yfinance's raw
  miss lines are silenced.
- **`audit` over a pending election** reported MISMATCHED and FAILED
  for the account the run deferred; the account is left out and named,
  and the checklist's audit step is blocked on the election instead.
- **Checklist hints:** the closing "Next" line follows a blocked step's
  own remedy (the first checklist said "download the exports" while the
  step asked for `taxjson run`); a `! ` line names the command for the
  problem, not the step's first command (a missing `local_timezone`
  said `tjs migrate`); in a year folder the exports folder is named as
  `../inputs/<account>/`.
- **`init` on a machine whose `/etc/timezone` says UTC** beside an
  `/etc/localtime` link to a real zone left `local_timezone`
  commented; the link's zone is taken (`TZ`, when set, still decides).
- **Single-folder project:** `years` and `new-year` point at
  `taxjson migrate --to-years` instead of a `new-year` that refuses.
- **`sanity` with no holdings file at all** names the unchecked
  accounts and exits 0, as commands.md said, instead of an error.
- **A headless run** said "but --no-input" when no flag was given: the
  message now says `--no-input` or "no terminal to answer on".
- **`run` wrote an empty `manifest.json`** into every account folder of
  a project reading its own `inputs/` (a frozen year's committed copy
  included); nothing is written until an election is saved.
- **`compare` exits 2** when there is nothing to compare with (no
  `reports/`, no run kept yet, no such snapshot); 1 stays "a report
  differs".

## v0.30.4 (2026-10-15)

### Added

- `taxjson option-yield [UNDERLYING...] [PERIOD] [ACCOUNT]`: how your
  option trades on an underlying did over a window — contracts written
  and bought, premiums received and paid, the realized profit or loss of
  the contracts closed in it and how they closed (expired, bought back,
  assigned, sold, exercised), the win rate, what is still open, and the yield on the
  cost of the underlying's shares you hold (on the strike notional
  where you hold none), annualized (`tjs option-yield QQQ 1y`). Planning numbers only (CA-PLAN-07 /
  US-PLAN-08): the tax treatment of each premium stays in the gains.

- `taxjson win-rates [SYMBOL...] [PERIOD] [ACCOUNT] [--by symbol|account|month|class]`:
  the win rate of every closed trade in the window per ticker (an
  option under its underlying), account, month of the close or asset
  class — trades, wins, losses, win rate, net P/L, average win and
  loss, profit factor — on the trades and the economic P/L `taxjson
  stats` counts (`tjs win-rates QQQ 1y`, `tjs win-rates --by month`).

- `taxjson plot-tax`: an ASCII chart of the tax the year's investment
  income generated month by month, against the year's estimate — the
  estimator `taxjson estimate` uses, run through each month's end on
  the same inputs, a month's tax the difference; the table under it has
  each month's income, tax and the running total (CA-PLAN-08 /
  US-PLAN-09). Planning numbers only.

### Changed

- v0.30.3 was tagged but never published: this release replaced it
  before its publish wait ended, with that wait shortened from 24 hours
  to one (`wait_hours` in `publish.toml`). This release carries its
  changes too.
- v0.30.2 was tagged but never published: the publisher's scan stopped
  it on the project's contact address, which is meant to be public.
  This release carries the same changes.
- **Releases reach this repository through a gated, delayed publisher.**
  Development moved to a private repository. Each release is now one
  commit here (`Release vX.Y.Z`) with its tag, published an hour after
  it is tagged and after two scans for personal data; the GitHub release
  is created by `.github/workflows/release.yml` from the CHANGELOG
  section. Channel moves (`channels.json`) follow on the publisher's next run,
  with no wait. Nothing
  in how taxjson computes changes, and installs upgrade as before.
- Pull requests are still welcome here; the maintainer lands them in the
  development repository and they ship with the next release
  (CONTRIBUTING.md).
- `scripts/release.sh` no longer takes `--notes FILE`: the release notes
  are always the CHANGELOG section.

### Fixed

- **Results audit (2026-10).** Thirteen findings, each pinned by
  tests/test_fix_result_audit_2026_10.py:
  - Canada: a merger with per-account ratios on shares renamed into
    the merger's source earlier was not folded (no weights were found
    behind the rename), so the first account's ratio renamed the whole
    pool: fewer shares held, a smaller gain on their sale. The weights
    now replay the renames (CA-CORP-13).
  - `taxjson stats` (and `win-rates`): a written option's buy-back
    entered with a negative amount counted as money received, and a
    split or renamed series lost its close; money is read as a
    magnitude and splits move the queued contracts (CA-RPT-16).
  - `taxjson div-estimate`: a short forward window (`1m`) truncated the
    rest-of-year total; the projection now runs to the year's end.
  - In this release's new commands: the T1135 merger fold follows the
    trade-date basis; `option-yield` finds a renamed series by its new
    underlying, keeps an unknown premium unknown in the totals (no
    realized P/L, win rate or yield instead of a loss), adds each
    underlying's own capital in the combined yield, and leaves earlier
    windows alone when a later split comes (lots keep their dated
    splits; the CLOSED and OPEN tables name each row's currency);
    `div-estimate --date` reads the books as of that date before
    netting a reversal or borrowing a share count; `plot-tax` labels
    cent-sized levels in cents and fits a 40-column terminal.
- `taxjson divs` / `events` / `trades` / `roc`: a dividend row with
  withholding on the row itself (IB) carries one more field, its net
  amount; when the listing's first row had fewer fields, that row's
  account and action were squeezed into one cell and its columns
  shifted left. The row views now align without a header: the columns
  lined up, a single-space gap, every row's fields in place.
- Kraken Earn rewards with a same-coin commission: the net quantity was
  `gross - fee` in binary floating point (`0.0025688399999999998`); it
  is now the ledger's decimal difference (`0.00256884`). The row views
  (`events`, `divs`, ...) write every quantity and rate out in full,
  never `5e-08`.
- `taxjson div-estimate`: a regular payer with a special beside the
  regular payment, a second broker's posting, a later-dated reversal or
  rows with no share count read `irregular`; the frequency is now the
  grid most of the last payments fall on (weekly added), a reversal
  nets against the payment it cancels, a row without a share count
  takes the account's nearest, and a single payment shows `1 payment`.
- **Filing figures (2026-10 audit).** Five defects changed exported
  amounts; each had a regression test added
  (tests/test_fix_filing_audit_2026_10.py):
  - US: a merger whose accounts received different whole-share ratios
    (12 old became 12 new, 40 became 42) applied the first account's
    ratio to every account's lots; the other account then sold more
    shares than it held and Form 8949 understated its gain (a phantom
    short). Each row now reaches its own account's lots (US-CORP-14);
    without per-account basis the rows fold as Canada's do.
  - US: a stock dividend's §307 basis spread reached a lot bought after
    the record date. It now reaches the lots entitled to it (bought
    before the row's `ex_date` / `record_date`); a broker's row without
    a date keeps the pay-date spread and warns about a lot bought within
    the 90 days before the pay date (US-STKDIV-01, US-STKDIV-04).
  - Canada: a superficial loss on a coin position below a millionth of
    a unit was denied but never added to the replacement's cost
    (Schedule 3 overstated the gain by the denied amount): the
    adjustment used the share tolerance that reads such a position as
    empty.
  - T1135: a merger's per-account ratios were replayed raw into the
    cost walk (fewer shares than delivered, too much cost released on
    a sale; CA-CORP-13); a coin held below a millionth of a unit was
    dropped from the property list and the cost amounts.
- Installer: `TAXJSON_DRY_RUN=1` with no install yet cloned the repository
  into `TAXJSON_DIR` and left it there. It now resolves the channel in a
  temporary clone removed on exit and never creates the install folder; on
  an existing install a dry run only fetches tags. The dev channel's dry
  run prints `channel dev → main`.

## v0.30.1 (2026-10-12)

### Changed

- v0.30.1 is v0.30.0 again, under a new number. The GitHub repository
  was recreated on 2026-10-12 so that pull requests from before v0.30.0
  no longer serve the withdrawn history, and GitHub does not let a
  published release's tag name be used again. Nothing in how taxjson
  computes changes. Issue and pull request numbers start again from 1:
  the numbers older entries below cite ("audit 81") are the earlier
  repository's, which is no longer public.

## v0.30.0 (2026-10-11)

### Changed

- The public history starts again from a single commit holding the
  same files, and releases v0.15.0 to v0.29.2 were withdrawn (personal
  data in old file versions and commit messages). Nothing in how
  taxjson computes changes; see docs/upgrading.md for pinned installs
  and old clones.

### Fixed

- Canada: a superficial loss whose replacement shares were still held
  under an old ticker, and came into the loss's symbol by a later
  rename or merger after that symbol had been sold out, is now added to
  the ACB of those shares, so their sale recovers it. Before, the loss
  was denied and never recovered, and the gains were overstated by the
  denied amount. The US engine was not affected. (audit 91)
- Coinbase: two identical purchases or sales in the same second, in an
  export whose ID column is blank on those rows, are now booked as two
  trades; they were read as one, so the gain was understated and a later sale
  showed a short position. A row without an ID is now told apart the
  way rows of an export with no ID column always were, and the same rows
  in an overlapping export are still counted once. Kraken rows with a
  blank `txid` get the same treatment (audit 93).
- One split reported twice (two brokers, or a `.tt` SPLIT line next to
  the broker's row, on dates a few days apart) is now one event in every
  step that walks splits. A sale executed before the split and settling
  after it was scaled by both copies when sizing a `[[distributions]]`
  row's record-date holding, so a reinvested distribution was booked too
  small and the gains came out too high; the same walk also skewed each
  account's share of a blended pool. (audit 92)
- The other views that walk splits count such a pair once too: the wash
  radar (it showed a short position after a sale settling across the
  split), `taxjson sanity`, `taxjson edge-cases`, `taxjson renames`, the
  cross-listing checks, the option checks and the opening-balance check.
  `taxjson splits` now marks the pair TWO-SOURCES (applied once) instead
  of TWICE?, and keeps TWICE? for the same ratio 8 to 10 days apart.

## v0.29.2 (2026-10-11)

### Changed

- `taxjson init --demo` now includes two more registered accounts, a
  LIRA at Questrade and an RRSP at Interactive Brokers, with share
  trades, dividends and a call sold at a loss, so its `sum` looks like a
  typical Canadian investor's. It also holds a fifth case: shares sold
  at a loss in a taxable account and bought back in the RRSP within 30
  days, a loss denied for good (`taxjson wash-sales`).

## v0.29.1 (2026-10-11)

### Fixed

- FX-on-cash ledger v2 (opt-in, under audit): a move between two of
  your own accounts (`CASHMOVE … own`) keeps its units and their cost in
  the one pooled average cost while it is in transit. Before, they left
  the pool until the receiving account recorded them, so a conversion in
  the meantime was costed without them and the figure depended on how
  long the move took. A move that arrives days later now gives the same
  figure as one that arrives the same day; a move into an account with a
  negative balance repays that debt at the pool's average cost. (audit 78)
- `taxjson audit --account <crypto account>` in a Canadian project with
  two or more crypto accounts recomputes with all of them, as the run
  pools the coins' cost across them; it used to re-run that one account
  alone and report a false mismatch (exit 1) on fresh books (audit 79).
- `taxjson-generate-parser`: the privacy gate now counts every kind of
  identity the redactor finds (a statement's bare preamble name, alias
  and address cells, and the lines it lists for review), refuses when
  the redactor would change any line of the sample, and sends only the
  redactor's copy of a sample that passed; it no longer sends the file's
  own text (audit 80). `taxjson redact` no longer counts a cell that
  already reads REDACTED as a finding.
- `taxjson fetch`: a broker's or proxy's error answer no longer shows the
  refresh token, access token, Flex token or an account number it
  echoes; the reason and body are scrubbed before they are printed
  (audit 81).
- Canada: a futures contract held in more than one taxable account is now
  averaged across all of them (s.47), as shares are: the same contracts in
  one account or split between two give the same gain. A long in one
  account and a short of the same contract in another are no longer
  netted, so each close is reported in the year its account closed it
  (it could move into the next year). Books with futures in one account
  are unchanged; US books are unchanged (FIFO within the account)
  (audit 76).
- An opening snapshot (`OPENING` line) dated inside the tax year no
  longer drops the gain of an earlier return of capital that went
  beyond the cost: the run stops and names the row, as it does for a
  left-out sale or short cover. The cost is walked back from the
  snapshot's (in a US project, a nil-basis lot bought before the
  return of capital counts too), so a return of capital the snapshot's
  cost shows stayed within it is still history the snapshot replaces.
  A `[[distributions]]` return of capital dated before a snapshot is
  now an ATTENTION line instead of a note (audit 77).
- An in-kind move of an LSE, JSE or Tel Aviv line valued from Yahoo's
  close is no longer booked at 100 times its value: the close keeps the
  unit Yahoo names (pence, cents, agorot) and is converted to pounds,
  rand or shekels, as current quotes already were; a close that names no
  unit (or one taxjson does not know) on those markets is not used, and
  closes cached by earlier releases for them are looked up again
  (audit 75).
- `harvest` no longer serves a cached price of another asset after a
  ticker.map `QUOTE` or `CRYPTO` line changes a symbol's Yahoo spelling:
  cache entries record the spelling they were fetched for, and one for
  another spelling (or from an earlier release, with none) is not used
  until it is fetched again online (audit 82).

### Changed

- Dependabot's weekly pip updates no longer open pull requests that
  edit the installer's locks (`requirements/`); the locks are
  regenerated with `scripts/lock_deps.py` instead.

## v0.29.0 (2026-10-11)

### Added (planning views)

- `taxjson rebuy`: every ticker sold at a loss whose repurchase window is
  still open, with the sale date, the loss, the accounts and the first
  day it can be bought back without the loss being denied (the days
  left). It is the wash radar's own date (Canada: the day after the
  window of the latest loss sale closes, 30 days after its settlement
  date; US: 31 days after its trade date), so `rebuy`, `wash-radar` and
  `buy-check` agree. A buy in any account counts, an RRSP, TFSA or IRA
  included (the loss is then denied for good); option series are listed
  under their underlying, each with its own date; listings ticker.map and
  tobase.map join count as one security. A ticker filter, `--date`,
  `--json`, `--details`; the windows that closed in the last 7 days are
  one line (tax-logic CA-PLAN-05 / US-PLAN-06). The radar's `--json`
  rows carry each recent loss (`losses`) and the re-entry date
  (`rebuy_at`); its new `--cleared-days N` lists the windows closed in
  the last N days too.
- `taxjson div-estimate`: upcoming dividends estimated from each held
  position's own dividend history in the books: the payment frequency
  (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, annual; irregular payers flagged),
  the latest and 12-month amount per share, the shares held now, the
  next pay date and amount; totals for the rest of the tax year and the
  next N months (`--months N` or a window such as `6m`), taxable and
  sheltered, in the base currency at the books' latest rate, with
  withholding where the books show a rate. Projected payments are dated
  by the same rule as `divs-sum`. Planning numbers only (tax-logic
  CA-PLAN-06 / US-PLAN-07).

### Changed (views)

- `taxjson winners` shows only the realized winners (gains above zero,
  best first, the top N); the new `taxjson losers` shows only the
  realized losers (below zero, worst first). One implementation: the
  same period / account positionals, `--top N`, `--json`, option
  grouping, and a taxable / sheltered line and a total for the side
  shown. `winners --json` is unchanged (every ticker, best first, the
  overall totals) and adds the side's own (`side_tickers`,
  `side_total_gain`, `side_total_gain_taxable`,
  `side_total_gain_sheltered`); `losers --json` is the same document
  ranked worst first.


## v0.28.4 (2026-10-10)

### Security

- The installer pins every dependency by hash. pip, setuptools, the core's dependencies and each extra (`fx` by default) come from the release's committed locks, `requirements/*.txt`, installed with `pip --require-hashes --only-binary :all:`. taxjson and taxjson-fetch are then installed from the release checkout with `--no-deps`. A package uploaded to PyPI after the lock was made cannot reach a new install. The unpinned `pip install --upgrade pip` is gone.
- A hash mismatch stops the installer with "A package pip downloaded does not match the sha256 that taxjson's lock … pins for it" and installs nothing unpinned instead (docs/troubleshooting.md). Only a missing wheel for the Python or platform still falls back to the core package, now with pinned dependencies and a warning that names the package. A network failure is no longer taken for a missing extra.
- A release older than the locks (`--channel v0.28.2`) is installed with main's locks.
- The locks cover Linux x86_64 and aarch64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, and Python 3.9 to 3.13. Nothing published in the last 7 days is locked. `scripts/lock_deps.py` regenerates them, and `tests/test_dependency_locks.py` fails when they no longer match `pyproject.toml` (docs/releasing.md, "Dependency locks").


## v0.28.3 (2026-10-10)

### Changed (release and CI, for maintainers)

- A release is two steps, so the commit that is tagged is one GitHub CI
  passed on: `scripts/release.sh vX.Y.Z --prepare` runs the full local
  gate, makes the version commit and lands it on `main` without a tag;
  `scripts/release.sh vX.Y.Z` (the cut) then refuses unless local `main`
  is `origin/main`, the version commit is on `main`, the tag is free and
  the `tests.yml` run for that commit's push to `main` passed (it waits
  for a run still going and names a failed one), and only then tags it
  and creates the GitHub release. Before, the tag was made seconds after
  the push, before CI had run.
- `main` is published through pull requests: `scripts/land.sh` runs the
  pre-push PII gate, pushes the new commits as a branch, opens a pull
  request, has it rebase-merged once its checks pass and brings local
  `main` to what landed; a failed check closes the pull request.
  `release.sh --prepare` and `promote.sh` publish `main` through it.
  docs/releasing.md has the ruleset (the required check names) and the
  emergency procedure.
- `release.sh` and `promote.sh` ask GitHub about CI the same way
  (`scripts/github-ci.sh`).

### Security

- gitleaks: the allowlist was a word list ("fake", "example",
  "synthetic", "placeholder"…) matched against each finding, which hid a
  real secret whose setting name held such a word. It is gone (a scan of
  the full history found no fixture that needs an exception); an
  exception is now an exact value for one rule in one file.
  `scripts/gitleaks-regression.sh` proves ordinary secrets are reported
  whatever they are called; on a pull request CI runs the base commit's
  copy of it against the proposed config, and scans with the base's
  config, so a pull request cannot widen either.
- The per-commit PII scan (patches, messages, identities) also runs on
  every push to `main`, over the pushed range, not only on pull requests.
- A daily "privacy watch" workflow scans what GitHub shows beside the code
  (recent issues, pull request titles and bodies, comments, release notes
  and commit messages) with the generic patterns and a read-only token:
  `scripts/check-public.sh --days N`.
- Every workflow action is pinned by commit SHA to a release that runs on
  Node 24 (actions/checkout v7.0.1, actions/setup-python v7.0.0, checked
  against their release tags), and every job runs on an explicit
  `ubuntu-24.04` runner instead of `ubuntu-latest`; a test refuses an
  unpinned action or a `*-latest` runner in any workflow.

### Fixed

- The docs said an immutable GitHub release's notes can never be edited.
  GitHub documents that only its assets and tag are locked; its title and
  notes stay editable. docs/releasing.md now says so and adds the
  procedure for something private that leaked into a release (in the
  notes, in an issue, or in code that shipped).
- A security test's control (a plain `git status` runs a hostile clean
  filter) was racy: git can call a file modified from its size alone
  without running the filter. The fixture now changes the file without
  changing its size, so git must read it through the filter every time.
- A `sell-check` test used fixed dates and failed once its loss sale was
  more than 30 days old (from 2026-10-11 UTC); its dates are now relative
  to the day it runs.


## v0.28.2 (2026-10-10)

### Added

- A project records the oldest taxjson its layout needs, `[settings]
  requires_taxjson = ">=X.Y.Z"`, and every command of an older taxjson
  stops before reading anything else with one line: "this project needs
  taxjson X.Y.Z or newer (installed: A.B.C)" (exit 2). An older release
  ignored a setting it did not know: a project with one shared
  tobase.map (`tobase_map`, v0.27.1) run with v0.27.0 read no tobase.map
  and failed on an unrelated line. `taxjson init` writes the release its
  layout needs (0.27.1 for a Canadian project of year folders, else
  0.27.0); `new-year`, `migrate` (the layout it migrated to),
  `update-tobase-map --write`, `find-missing-history
  --write-missing-history` and `align --write` raise it; none lowers it.
  A value that is not `">=X.Y.Z"` stops every command, naming the key.
- Every command, not only `taxjson run`, warns in one line about a
  `[settings]` key it does not read (a misspelling, or a setting of a
  newer taxjson).

### Fixed

- Every edit of taxjson.toml by `align`, `migrate` and `new-year` now reads the keys as TOML does and reads the result back: it must be the file with exactly that key changed, or the command stops and writes nothing (it never writes a file that reads differently).
- `migrate` (one shared tobase.map) sets `tobase_map` inside a `[settings]` inline table instead of adding a second `[settings]` table, and checks every year's edit before moving any file (audit 34).
- `align --write` checks every chosen change before writing: ticker.map is no longer changed when the taxjson.toml edit fails, and it is put back when the second write fails (audit 35).
- `align` and `years --diff` keep an account name holding a dot (`[accounts."margin.one"]`) as one name: its account ids and holdings stay out of the output, and the key is written in its own table (audit 36).
- `new-year` sets `year` whatever its spelling (`+2024`, `2_024`, `0x7e8`) (audit 37), in a `[settings]` inline table (audit 38), and puts `prior_year_record` in `[settings]` when the settings are dotted keys (audit 39).
- `new-year` makes the year's files in a staging folder and moves them into place only when complete: a failure no longer leaves a taxjson.toml that blocks running it again (audit 40).
- `align` adds and removes an array of tables (`[[distributions]]`): adding one wrote an invalid `[]` line, removing one kept it (audit 41).
- `align` and `years --diff` list the accounts' order when it differs (`accounts (order)`); align shows it and leaves the tables as they are (audit 42).
- `migrate --to-years` moves a holdings folder named by `holdings_dir` with the year (or names one further away from the year folder) (audit 43), and makes a moved ticker.map link by a relative path again from the year folder (audit 44).
- `align` and `years --diff` stop with an error naming a taxjson.toml or ticker.map that cannot be read, instead of reporting no differences; `years` lists it as that year's problem (audit 56).
- `new-year` in Canada sets `option_grant_timing_since` to the previous year when that year left it unset (on grant timing), so a premium written then and closed in the new year is not taxed again (audit 57).
- Rows of two accounts at the same moment follow the accounts' names, not their order in taxjson.toml: reordering the file changed gains without calling the books stale (CA-DATE-14 / US-DATE-13; a filed year with such a trade can show DRIFTED once) (audit 31).
- US: adding or removing a filed-year lock makes the books stale (`filed/ (locked years)`), since the gains read the locked years (US-WASH-22) (audit 32).
- `taxjson years` names a damaged `filed/<year>.json` ("lock damaged", with the problem) instead of showing the year as filed (audit 49).
- `taxjson option-boundary` on a base book without its rows stops with one error naming the file, not a traceback (audit 53).
- `taxjson wash-radar` and `taxjson-safe-to-sell` refuse a `--date` whose window leaves the calendar (9999-12-31) instead of a traceback (audit 54).
- The estimate says when its carried losses or minimum tax come from a lock taken before its year ended (provisional): one `!` line, the note with `--details` (audit 55).
- Command chaining: the folder after `-C` / `--dir` is never taken for the first command when it is named like one (`tjs -C run run sum`), and `tjs -C run` alone shows the help page (audit 51).
- Command chaining: an account, a folder or a symbol named like a command is the command's own argument where the command takes one (`tjs events sum` with an account named sum, `tjs init sum`, `tjs audit sum`); `--` always separates two commands (`tjs events -- sum`), and `tjs run sum` and `tjs fetch run` chain as before (audit 52).
- `tjs init` checks the folders it writes into before creating anything: an `inputs/` (or year folder) that is a symlink to outside the project is refused with nothing written, instead of receiving the account folders and READMEs (audit 45).
- `tjs sanity` and the end of `tjs run` accept a holdings snapshot of an account that holds nothing (a `[meta]` table and no `[[holding]]`, as the fetch plugin writes it once every position is closed) instead of stopping with "no [[holding]] array" (audit 46).
- A holdings/ snapshot is matched to its account by `[meta] broker_account` before `[meta] account`, so a fetched snapshot whose `account` still names a renamed account is claimed by the account declaring its broker id (audit 47).
- Two account names that differ only by letter case (`Margin` and `margin`) are refused with a message naming both: their folders and holdings snapshots could not be told apart, and one account received the other's positions (audit 48).
- `tjs elect ACCOUNT` (and `--json`) no longer lists the sheltered-default events of a longer-named account whose name starts with ACCOUNT and `_` (audit 50).
- The run's closing "accounts with positions not checked against the broker's holdings" line no longer counts an account whose `holdings/` snapshot the positions check found (by broker account id or file name) and compared; an account with no snapshot is still listed. `tjs sanity`'s `UNCHECKED:` line now says a holdings/ snapshot also counts.

### Security

- The pre-push hook scans every merge commit's own patch too (audit 33): a
  value that only a merge resolution wrote, and a later commit removed,
  is in the published history but was in neither the net diff nor the
  per-commit pass (`git log -p --no-merges`). The per-commit pass reads
  merges as combined diffs (`--cc`), and `scripts/check-pii.sh --diff`
  scans the lines a merge adds against every parent; lines a parent
  already had are that parent's commit's. The `pr-commits` CI job scans
  a pull request's merge commits (patch, message, identities) the same
  way; `scripts/release.sh` and `scripts/promote.sh` run the hook, so
  they get it too.
- `scripts/check-pii.sh --diff` (the pre-push hook, the `pr-commits`
  CI job) scans an added line whose text begins with `++ `: in a diff
  it reads `+++ …`, and it was taken for a file header and skipped by
  every pattern. Only a `+++ ` line in a file's header block, before its
  first hunk, is a header now.
- `scripts/promote.sh` no longer skips the pre-push PII gate when
  `scripts/hooks/pre-push` is not executable: it runs the hook through
  `bash`, and refuses before changing anything when the hook or
  `scripts/check-pii.sh` is missing. `scripts/release.sh` refuses the
  same way up front and runs the hook through `bash` too.


## v0.28.1 (2026-10-10)

### Fixed

- Tests: every test process runs with full-length messages (`TAXJSON_WIDTH=0` unless a test sets its own), as the local gate does, so GitHub CI and `scripts/ci.sh` agree again.
- Tests: the new-user tests start taxjson through the launcher that uses `-P` only on Python 3.11+, so they run on 3.9 and 3.10.


## v0.28.0 (2026-10-10)

### Added

- `taxjson init --demo [DIR]`: a project of made-up exports to try first
  (Canada, tax year 2024: two IB accounts, Questrade, Webull, a TFSA at
  RBC, Kraken and Coinbase), ready to run offline once the rates are
  cached, with the commands to try (`run`, `sum`, `checklist`). It holds
  the getting-started scenarios: a sale with no purchase, a spin-off
  with its election saved, a superficial loss and a written option open
  at the year end. `--country` is no longer required with `--demo`.

### Changed

- Essentials first: a command's default output is the essentials, said
  concisely (docs/output-style.md, "Essentials first"). A legend of one
  or two lines comes before the table it explains; after the data only
  the lines you must act on (starting `! `) or must not miss, one line
  each, naming the command with the detail; every explanation, caveat,
  rounding note and citation moved behind a new `--details` flag (or the
  topic command), nothing dropped. `--json` is unchanged.
- `taxjson sum`: the column legends before the tables; the sheltered
  accounts' scope in their headings; after FOR THE RETURN one `! ` line
  per warning (sales with no purchase, unknown costs, FX on foreign
  cash, §1256 contracts, ALLOWLOSS filing positions) and one line on
  slip capital gains; the long notes, the rounding notes and the
  FILING POSITIONS section are under `sum --details`. When the width
  drops the DENIED column, its total is in the legend.
- The report commands' "these books are not the clean result of the
  current inputs" and "built for another tax year" warnings are one
  line, naming `taxjson checklist` / `taxjson run`; `--details` lists
  the problems.
- `taxjson checklist` shows the essentials: the done count, one row per
  section with its counts, one line per step needing attention (its id,
  what was found and the command to run; steps blocked for one reason
  share a line), and the next step last. `--all` (or `--details`) is the
  full list with every step's state, commands and why. One progress line
  instead of one per check.
- Set-up commands print the essentials (docs/output-style.md, "Essentials
  first"); `--details` brings back everything they leave out.
  `taxjson init` and `taxjson new-year`: the project made and four next
  steps, one line each (the files written and the next-year hint with
  `--details`). `taxjson elect --pending`: a table of each event's options
  with the first clause of what each books and the hint it needs, and one
  `--set` line to copy (each option's full text and its own `--set` line
  with `--details`; the last line the checklist reads is unchanged).
  `taxjson redact` (no file): one line of totals and one line naming the
  free text to read (each file's counts with `--details`). `taxjson
  format`, `taxjson migrate` and `taxjson crypto-sends`: one-line notes
  and legends.
- Essentials first for the summaries: `taxjson estimate`, `amt`,
  `instalments`, `carryover`, `t1135`, `fx-cash`, `form-export` and
  `reconcile-slips` print a short legend above each table, the figures
  for the return, and one line per thing to act on (`! ...`) naming the
  command with the detail. The notes, caveats, citations and per-row
  explanations they printed after the data moved behind `--details`
  (nothing was dropped). `taxjson estimate` shows the estimate alone
  (the gains table is `taxjson sum`; `--details` puts it back in
  front); `reconcile-slips` lists one row per symbol with the first
  clause of its finding. The standalone stage tools keep their full
  reports (`--brief` gives the short one); `--json` is unchanged.
- The check commands print the essentials first (docs/output-style.md):
  `sanity`, `find-missing-history`, `slip-audit`, `edge-cases`,
  `close-year`, `ticker-map --suggest`, `check-dates`,
  `update-tobase-map` and `option-boundary` keep their tables and figures, put a one-line legend
  above a table that needs one, and end with one-line `! ` items naming
  the command with the detail. The explanations, fix steps, per-row
  reasoning, notes and empty sections they printed before are behind
  the new `--details` flag; nothing was dropped. `--json` is unchanged.
- `taxjson years` is a table, one row per year (state, totals, last
  run, changed inputs, what differs from the newest year), with one
  line per thing to do; `--details` prints each year in words as
  before.
- `taxjson run`'s console shows each warning and note as one line that
  names the command with the detail (an error keeps its fix lines); the
  closing block under "Before you trust these numbers" is at most six
  lines, every finding kept. The broker each file was read as, and every
  message's explanation, come back with `taxjson run --details` (and stay
  in work/*.diag); output captured by a program is unchanged.
- The trading and loss commands print the essentials first: a one-line
  legend above each table, then only what to act on (`! ` lines naming
  the command with the detail) and a closing pointer to `--details`,
  which prints everything the default view leaves out. `wash-sales`
  (WHAT DENIED MEANS, the filing positions and manual-check flags in
  full), `wash-radar` (now one STATUS table of the positions with an
  advisory and an action line per status; the definitions, empty
  sections and per-row advisories are the details), `harvest` (the
  column notes), `audit` (the rounding note), `buy-check` / `sell-check`
  (the window caveat), `transfers` (the IN_BOOKS meanings), `list`,
  `stats` and `fees-sum` (the definitions). The planning views close
  with the scope in a few words (the purchases of a spouse or a
  controlled corporation are not checked); `--details` keeps the full
  paragraph. `--json` and the run's reports/ files are unchanged.
- The note on option roots whose contract size the export does not
  state is one line when it names three roots or fewer.
- The messages a command's engine prints while it recomputes (an
  income-year note of an earlier year, a built-in list note) are one
  line each in the default view, and one said more than twice is folded
  into a count line at the end; `--details` shows each in full.
- `taxjson help` lists the maintainer's release commands (`channels`,
  `deploy`, `promote`, now under "Maintainer") only on a development
  checkout; `taxjson help --all` lists them everywhere, and they still run.
- A new `taxjson.toml` leaves `option_grant_timing_since` commented out
  with a one-line explanation (it matters only once you write options),
  unless another year folder beside it sets it. `taxjson run` warns that
  it is not set only when the books hold a written option, and warns in
  one line when it is later than `year`.
- `taxjson init` from January to April adds one line: filing last year?
  The command for its folder (the default stays the calendar year).

### Fixed

- `taxjson close-year` no longer locks a year while checklist steps
  before the lock need attention: it lists them and asks on a terminal;
  without one it refuses unless `--yes`.
- The installer's closing recipe built `~/taxes/2026/2026/`: it is now
  `mkdir -p ~/taxes && cd ~/taxes && tjs init --country canada && cd
  2026`. `taxjson init` in an empty folder named like a year refuses,
  naming the command for the folder above it (`--single` still works
  there).
- `taxjson run` no longer says "the same broker account feeds two taxjson
  accounts" for two different brokers' exports that print the same
  account number: the check keys on the broker and the number.
- The broker demo exports (`examples/*_demo.csv`) each carry their own
  synthetic account id; the Webull demo no longer settles on a Sunday and
  the Questrade demo no longer trades on an NYSE holiday.
- `taxjson run` downloads exchange rates only from a few days before the
  earliest date in the project's files (never later than January 1 of the
  year), not from 2000: a recent project no longer fetches decades of
  Bank of Canada rates, nor Yahoo Finance for the years before the Bank's
  series.
- A `.tt` line whose symbol has no market suffix (`AAPL` where the broker
  rows hold `AAPL.US`) is a pool of its own: `taxjson run` now says so on
  the console, naming the file:line and the listing the books hold (the
  warning reached only the `.sum`, and not even that with exports shared
  by every year).
- Text that contradicted v0.27.x: `tips --online` no longer advises a
  `DISTINCT` line for a depositary receipt (look-alike listings are never
  joined); `init` and `new-year` (help and output) say tobase.map is one
  file beside the year folders, not copied per year (and a US project's
  `init` no longer mentions it); `run -h` names `inputs_dir` and the
  holdings/ snapshots found without a setting; the account folders'
  README says each year's slips go in `YYYY/inputs/slips/`.
- Help text that contradicted the program: `renames -h` names the `.tt`
  line `RENAME YYYY-MM-DD OLD NEW late=fold|late=separate` (not the legacy
  ticker.map form); `sanity -h` says that with no items it reads the
  year's holdings/ snapshots without a setting; `estimate -h` gives the
  real defaults of `--other-income` and `--other-losses` (the
  `[estimate]` keys, then the latest close-year lock); `init -h` says
  `--country` is not needed with `--demo`.
- `taxjson wash-sales --explain` no longer says "no matching gains
  found" under a traced denial when another book (a crypto account's)
  has none; the note appears once, only when no book has a denial.
- The Canadian tax estimate (`taxjson sum --other-income`, `taxjson
  estimate`) taxes the RETURN row's gain, the per-disposition cents you
  file; it showed the unrounded engine total, a cent or so apart.

### Docs

- README.md is a front page (what taxjson is, status, install, a
  five-minute start, brokers, what it does and does not do, privacy,
  getting help, a docs index and a one-line-per-command index). Its
  reference material moved to its canonical page: new docs/commands.md
  (every command in detail), new docs/brokers.md (each broker's downloads
  with the brokers' help pages cited, broker detection, the generic
  importer, the fetch plugin, tax slips), docs/settings.md and
  docs/tax-rules.md (configuration, project files and rule explanations),
  docs/getting-started.md (missing history), SECURITY.md (egress) and
  CONTRIBUTING.md (development setup, running the stages by hand).
- New docs/upgrading.md (channels, what to do after an upgrade, every
  change that asks something of you by release, and the problems an
  upgrade alone fixes), docs/limits.md (what taxjson does not do; Canada
  supported, US experimental) and docs/glossary.md. The knowledge-pack
  test checks the new pages' paths, symbols and commands.
- The deck (docs/deck/) is brought up to date: the year folders, shared
  inputs/ and tobase.map; real `tjs wash-sales` output from the demo
  project on the worked example; the test count docs/limits.md states;
  the commands slide rendered from the help page's groups
  (`scripts/deck_commands.py`); the privacy slide's dependency and
  network wording as SECURITY.md has it; the brokers as docs/brokers.md
  names their downloads; a first run that starts with `tjs init --demo`.
  `scripts/build_deck.sh` renders the PDF with WeasyPrint 70.0 and
  records the HTML's hash, and a test fails when the PDF was not rebuilt.
- SECURITY.md lists every network call with what it sends, including the
  Yahoo Finance closes for in-kind moves between taxable and registered
  accounts and for crypto-send values.
- CONTRIBUTING.md: setup with `scripts/dev-setup.sh`, the pull-request
  checklist reads `scripts/ci.sh`'s PASS line, and the fetcher contract
  names `FetchRequest.inputs` / `holdings`.
- The README, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md and the bug-report template
  say the same about sharing a file: never a raw export; a made-up
  reproduction first; a `taxjson redact` copy only after reading all of it.
- docs/troubleshooting.md keeps the problems you can still meet; the
  ones an upgrade alone fixes are listed by release in docs/upgrading.md.
  KNOWN_ISSUES.md lists open bugs only; limitations moved to
  docs/limits.md.
- examples/README.md: the stage-by-stage run sets `TAXJSON_LOCAL_TZ` for
  the crypto demos and shows the current summary labels.
- The 2026-07 audit reports at the repository root are removed (their
  findings are fixed and recorded in this changelog).


## v0.27.2 (2026-10-10)

### Fixed

- Docs: the examples in KNOWN_ISSUES.md and README.md use made-up figures.


## v0.27.1 (2026-10-10)

### Changed

- Multi-year projects (Canada): one `tobase.map` beside the year folders
  that every year reads, through a new `[settings] tobase_map =
  "../tobase.map"` (the path must stay inside the folder holding the
  years, like `inputs_dir`). `taxjson init` writes it there and sets the
  key, `taxjson new-year` keeps the key (no per-year copy), and
  `taxjson update-tobase-map` in any year folder, or in the folder
  holding them, updates that one file and says it applies to every
  year. Each year's ticker.map still wins over it. A change to the
  shared file shows in every year's run banner, `taxjson years` and the
  checklist as `../tobase.map (shared by every year)`, so a filed
  year's drift check catches what it moved. Single-folder projects keep
  tobase.map beside ticker.map.
- `taxjson migrate` (in the folder holding the years, or a year folder)
  makes the per-year copies earlier versions wrote one shared file:
  identical copies at once (each kept as `tobase.map.bak`); copies that
  differ are listed with the lines of yours only an older copy has, and
  need `--write` (the newest year's file is kept). A year folder that
  has the setting and still holds a tobase.map of its own is refused,
  naming both. `taxjson years` and `taxjson align` compare the setting,
  not the file; `migrate --to-years` keeps tobase.map at the top.
- tobase.map no longer carries `DISTINCT` lines for a Canadian
  depositary receipt (CDR): taxjson never joins two listings because
  their letters match, so look-alike listings need no line.
  `taxjson update-tobase-map --write` retracts the ones earlier versions
  wrote ("not needed: look-alike listings are never joined"; a line you
  edited is kept and flagged). The interlisted master still knows each
  CDR: in a Canadian project a broker's journal between a CDR and its US
  share is never joined (a `.tt` JOURNAL line between them stops the
  run), and neither `ticker-map --suggest`, a MAP-GAP nor the
  cross-listing loss radar pairs them (tax-logic CA-XLIST-06).

### Fixed

- A `.tt` `OPENING … cost=unknown` line follows ticker.map and tobase.map
  as the rows do: a line naming a TOBASE listing opens the security in the
  base-currency books (it was dropped and the later trades became short
  covers) and the listing the books trade in the native holdings view; a
  mapping added after the line is followed too (audit 23).
- A dated `OPENING … cost=unknown` line's units are held even when no
  later row trades them (a holding kept, or one that only pays
  dividends): in the gains inventory, the holdings report, `sanity` and
  `t1135` (audit 24).
- `taxjson migrate` dates each entry from the books of the year folder
  that sized it (an account only an older year has), and renames no
  `missing_history.json` while an entry cannot be converted: it stops
  naming them (audit 25).
- `taxjson migrate` lets the newest year listing an entry decide it: an
  explicit "opens nothing" there is no longer replaced by an older year's
  opening; a year that does not list it does not decide (audit 28).
- `taxjson redact` in a year folder with shared exports copied the year's
  taxjson.toml, ticker.map and tobase.map unredacted: an account id found
  only in the configuration (`account`, `broker_accounts`, `query_id`), a
  denylist or `--also` match found only in those files and contact details
  in their comments stayed in the copy, and `--check` said "Nothing to
  redact". They are now redacted (an id with the same placeholder as in
  the exports, so the copy still runs) and counted; in a single-folder
  project an id only taxjson.toml names is replaced in the exports too
  (audit 22).
- `taxjson redact` read a Questrade option description such as `CALL QZP
  09/18/26 40 QZERO SQUARE ...` as a street address and replaced the strike
  and issuer, so the copy's run read the option as shares and stopped on
  a price × quantity mismatch. A number right after an option's expiry is
  no house number now. And every redacted export is read again by its
  parser and compared with the original: if any row count, quantity,
  price or amount would differ, nothing is written (exit 2, naming the
  file and the row).
- A taxjson.toml value written over several lines (a `holdings = [...]`
  list with one file per line, a multi-line string) was only partly
  rewritten by `taxjson redact`, `align --write` and `migrate --to-years`:
  the first line replaced, the rest left behind, so the copy did not read
  as TOML. The whole value is now replaced or commented out, and redact
  checks the copied file reads before writing anything (audit 26).
- `taxjson new-year` missed an account table named in quotes or with a
  hyphen (`[accounts."margin-main"]`, `[accounts.margin-main]`): last
  year's `holdings` list stayed active in the new year (and could
  override its snapshots), or lines of the account were commented out
  when the table before it was [estimate] or [instalments] (audit 27).
- `slip-audit --import-cra`: the 60-second limit on pdftotext covered
  only reading its output; a pdftotext that closed its output and kept
  running was waited for without a limit. The limit now covers its exit
  too, and it is killed and reaped when it passes (audit 29).


## v0.27.0 (2026-10-09)

### Added

- Interlisted shares (Canada): taxjson ships a master of Canadian shares
  that also trade in the United States under the same share class (a TSX
  or TSX Venture line, its US exchange listing and its US OTC listings),
  each pair checked against OpenFIGI's share-class FIGI and the Nasdaq
  Trader symbol directory; depositary receipts are never paired. A
  Canadian project carries its pairs as `tobase.map` beside ticker.map
  (`taxjson init --country canada` writes it, `taxjson new-year` copies
  it): read as if its `TOBASE` lines were in ticker.map, so the two
  listings are one ACB pool and one security for the superficial-loss
  rule (tax-logic CA-XLIST-06). ticker.map wins over it, with an Info
  line when the two disagree. A US project does not read it (US-XLIST-05).
- `taxjson update-tobase-map [--write] [--json]`: what a newer master
  adds, ends (`until`, never deleted) or retracts, the ticker changes
  (nothing to write when the old and new tickers already book under the
  same listing; else the dated `.tt` RENAME event to write) and the pairs
  your ticker.map decides otherwise; without a tobase.map, which pairs
  would change the books (read over their full history, every year the
  exports hold). Dry run by default. Your edits are kept: a marked line
  whose rule you changed (another target, the direction reversed) is
  yours, and the master's line for the same listing is not added beside
  it; a master line you delete stays deleted (recorded as a `# removed:`
  line); your comment lines and lines that are not `TOBASE` / `DISTINCT`
  are kept (the latter listed). `--write` also creates an empty
  ticker.map when there is none. A new checklist item says when
  tobase.map is older than the installed master, and `taxjson years`
  counts the tobase.map lines that differ between years.
- A row in an ended interlisting after its `until` date is a Warning
  naming the possible reuse of the ticker; when the master knows the
  ticker names another security today, every row of it is a Warning,
  whatever its date.
- The interlisted master's corrections: a listing shipped in error is
  retracted for good (with its reason) and `update-tobase-map` removes
  its line unless you edited it (an edited one is kept and flagged). The
  maintainer's build refuses an ended US ticker that names another
  security today unless the reuse is recorded. This release retracts an
  ended pair's wrong US ticker (another company's ADR), moves an ended
  trust's US line to the share class it traded under, ends an OTC ticker
  of an issuer's former name, adds three ended pairs (a former Nasdaq
